and he did so to display an ever-great marvel to those who pride themselves on their devotion to knowledge.

Then Hari assumed the form of a tortoise so that the gods and demons, while churning the ocean, might hold Mount Mandara upon his back; for that Great-Souled One is capable of supporting even the entire universe.
Then the Great-Souled Hari appeared, named Dhanvantari, with the luster of an emerald,
holding in his hand a full pitcher of nectar, solely for the purpose of warding off the defects of unwholesome food.
Then the Great-Souled Hari assumed that form of Śrī which people in the world call Mohinī, in order to completely deceive the power of those arrogant sons of Diti.
Then the great-souled Lord Hari appeared, the infinite Blessed One named Nṛsiṃha;
and the Daitya Hiraṇyakaśipu was likewise pinned to his thighs and torn asunder by his claws.
Then the Blessed Lord Hari, the god of gods, became a dwarf through Aditi from Kaśyapa;
O lord of birds, he did so desiring to give this [earth] to Indra, and for the sake of purifying and protecting it.
Then Hari became the son of Jamadagni, whom everyone in the world calls Paraśurāma;
O Lord of Heroes, the Great Lord desired to rid the earth of the Kṣatriyas who were hostile to Brahmins.
Thereupon, that Viṣṇu, being complete, assumed the form of Vyāsa four times for the sake of Rāghava;
he was born from Parāśara upon Satyavatī in order to divide the portions of the Vedas among Paila and the others.
Then, O lord of heroes, Rāghava— the lion among monkeys who descended from the solar dynasty into the lineage of Raghu through Kausalyā—
was capable of engaging in battle with the ocean and of slaying Rāvaṇa and the others upon the earth.
Then, in the twenty-eighth Dvāpara age, the Lord Hari became Vyāsa in the form of knowledge;
the Great-Souled God himself appeared from Parāśara and Satyavatī in order to divide the Vedas.
Then Hari, that Viṣṇu, desiring to utterly destroy Kaṃsa and the others, and wishing to fully protect the Pāṇḍavas, O lord of heroes, became manifest as Kṛṣṇa from Vasudeva upon Devakī.

Then, O Lord of Birds, when the Kali age had fully set in, Hari was born among the Kīkaṭas by the name of Buddha for the purpose of deluding the asuras, solely in order to reject the authority of the Vedas.
Then, at the junction between the two ages, Hari, the lord of heroes known as Kalki,
will be born in the house of Viṣṇugupta under the name Hari, in order to slay those kings who are mostly robbers.
The twenty-four beginning with Keśava, the [twenty-four] beginning with Saṃkarṣaṇa, the thousand beginning with Viśva, and those beginning with Para are recorded as being infinite.
For the incarnations of Viṣṇu, also known as Nārāyaṇa, are indeed innumerable;
yet they are themselves Nārāyaṇas, differing from him not even in the slightest degree.
Furthermore, Viṣṇu is infinite in his strength, form, qualities, and in every way; he is full of infinite attributes and not otherwise.
Thus ends the fifteenth chapter, titled "The Description of the Incarnations of Viṣṇu," in the Brahma-kāṇḍa, the third part of the Uttara-khaṇḍa of the glorious Garuḍa Mahāpurāṇa.
In the glorious Garuḍa Mahāpurāṇa, Chapter 16,
Śrī Kṛṣṇa said:
O Lord of Birds, O highly fortunate one, listen properly to the true nature and the incarnations of Mahālakṣmī, as well as the definitive conclusion regarding the knowledge thereof. GarP_3,16.1 //
For the eye of the Self alone perceives the world as other than Īśa;
that which makes it its object is proclaimed to be the knowledge of Lakṣmī.
The Goddess who is eternally inseparable [from Him], whose sole refuge is the foot of Hari, who is eternally liberated and eternally awakened, is proclaimed as Mahālakṣmī. (GarP 3.16.3)
And Lakṣmī is proclaimed as the wife of Hari, the Root;
for the wife of the Puruṣa is Prakṛti, and she is the presiding deity of Prakṛti.
O Lord Indra, in order to perform creation together with the Puruṣa through the qualities (guṇas), she who was then called Prakṛti likewise began to drink the darkness (tamas). 3,16.5.
The wife of Vāsudeva is celebrated by the name Māyā,
while the wife of Saṃkarṣaṇa is proclaimed as Jayā.
The wife of Aniruddha was celebrated by the name Śāntā;
Kṛti, the wife of Pradyumna, also became intent on creating offspring.
The goddess Śrī is celebrated as the consort of Viṣṇu and is considered the embodiment of *sattva*;
Durgā is proclaimed as the embodiment of *tamas* and is known as Kanyā.
In the Kṛṣṇa incarnation, she was indeed like a maiden, the younger sister of Nanda’s son;
as the goddess Earth, she was possessed by Rajas and became the wife of the Boar.
Vīndra, who presides over the Vedas, is proclaimed as Annapūrṇā;
she is remembered as the unborn Lakṣmī, the wife of Nārāyaṇa.
The wife of Hari, who is known as Sacrifice (Yajña), is proclaimed to be Dakṣiṇā.
Jayantī is celebrated as the wife of Vṛṣabha alone;
Sītā, the daughter of Videha, is proclaimed as the wife of Rāma.
Rukmiṇī and Satyabhāmā are celebrated as the two wives of Kṛṣṇa;
indeed, his incarnations are infinite and of various kinds.
O best of Brahmins, they exist as mutually non-different from one another;
yet they are proclaimed to be inferior to Viṣṇu, who possesses infinite and infinite qualities.
Now, Brahmā and Vāyu are inferior by ten million times to Śrī;
O best of the lords of birds, listen as I describe the form of Brahmā.
O Lord of Birds, he who was produced from Vāsudeva through Māyā is that very one named Puruṣa, celebrated as Viriñca.
From Aniruddha, however, when Śāntā was present, the body of the Great Principle (mahattattva) came into being;
at that time, O Lord of Birds, it received the name Mahān Virañci.
O best of birds, he who was born here from Vāsudeva through Māyā and the quality of passion (rajas), known as Vidhi, is to be understood as Viriñca.
O best of birds, he who was born within the cosmic egg as Padmanābha and became the one seated upon the lotus (Kamalāsana) also acquired the designation of the Four-faced One (Caturmukha).
Thus the four forms of Brahmā have been proclaimed;
now I shall speak of the names of Vāyu—listen, O best of the lords of birds.
And he who was born from Saṃkarṣaṇa in Jayā is to be known as Vāyu, the first, and is celebrated as Pradhāna.
Because he bestows worldly activity, he is celebrated by the name of the Sūtra;
and for the sake of praising Viṣṇu while he resides at Badarī with steadfastness, he [is so called].
Vāyu assumed the form of fortitude (dhṛti); therefore, he is remembered as Dhṛti.
He abides in the form of fortitude for those who are fit and devoted to Hari.
Since the wind residing in the heart is indeed known as *dhṛti*,
it remains in the hearts of all and constantly remembers Hari.
Therefore, O best of birds, he came to be known as Vāyu-sthiti;
or rather, Vāyu alone [went] to Hari residing in Śvetadvīpa.
O Lord of the Vedas, he is indeed always remembered; therefore, he is known as Smṛti.
And because he is known by Viṣṇu through his proclamation, he dwells within the hearts of all.
Therefore, by my command, it was indeed the wind itself that became known to me as "Liberation" (Mukti), without a doubt; through the gateway of knowledge, it bestows liberation upon devotees.
For that very wind, alone, bearing the name "Liberation," abiding in the hearts of devotees, increases their devotion to Viṣṇu.
Therefore, he is celebrated as a devotee of Viṣṇu; there is no doubt about this.
He is indeed the very consciousness of the minds of all living beings.
Since wind is of the nature of mind, it is therefore remembered as "mind";
he is the sovereign of all sovereigns and of all those who are brothers to Garuḍa.
Therefore, O best of beings, Vāyu alone is remembered as the great lord;
abiding within the hearts of all, he beholds their strength.
Therefore, O son of Vinatā, you have obtained the name "Bala" (Strength);
and by dwelling in the hearts of all people through your sons, grandsons, and descendants, you shall remain so.
Because he constantly performs sacrifices, he is known as the Sacrificer (Yaṣṭṛ);
this has been so from infinite kalpas until the very end of time.

There is no crookedness in yoga; it is remembered as being "straight" (ṛju). What is called "crookedness" in yoga is the desire for rewards in the worship of Hari, or the worship of Hari performed out of desire for the status of Īśa, Rudra, and so forth.
Furthermore, O Lord of Birds, for some [beings] they are therefore remembered as crooked.
Even among the sages and others, there is the worship of Hari performed for the sake of specific desires;
therefore, they should not be considered straightforward, so what need is there to mention ordinary humans? (GarP 3.16.36)
As long as that best of men does not abandon his desired worship,
so too do the sages and others [abandon] that which is an obstacle to liberation.
Since beginningless time, there has been a latent impression (*vāsanā*) produced by karma;
who is it that all those entitled to liberation worship? (GarP 3.16.38)
And having obtained that yoga from a teacher who awakens one's consciousness— though it was almost entirely lost—
and having practiced it thoroughly, one shall attain liberation at the end.
Worship of Viṣṇu performed for the sake of desire bestows sovereignty, yet it results in perverted knowledge; by that, one goes to the lower darkness.
If that very same thing is proclaimed as being the opposite for the sake of knowledge—
just as the perception of Viṣṇu toward a stone is likewise the perception of Viṣṇu toward a twice-born brahmin.
O Lord of Birds, one should likewise perceive the notion of a sacred ford in water,
and similarly perceive Viṣṇu in Śiva, the Sun, and the six-faced Kārttikeya.
All such primordial knowledge is traditionally held to be erroneous; rather, one should contemplate all things, beginning with stone, as being identical [with the Self]. (GarP 3.16.43)
It is said that this is the "perception of Viṣṇu," but not the awareness of being situated therein;
even throughout beginningless and endless time, one may worship Hari with desire.
Because it does not exist [in other directions], the wind is proclaimed to be straight and suitable;
for others, it never exists, and therefore they are remembered as not being straight.
Or rather, it always reveals Hari directly to those who are qualified for liberation at the proper time; therefore, it is called "wisdom" (prajñā).
Even beyond the reach of the senses, he always causes Hari to be seen by all;
therefore, O Lord of the Vindhyas, Vāyu is eternally celebrated as Knowledge itself.
Because he instructs his devotees on what is beneficial and what is harmful, that Wind-god dwells within their hearts; and for that reason, he also received the designation of "Guru."
Abiding in the hearts of yogis, he meditates upon the supreme Hari;
even while meditating upon him as distinct [from himself], he is remembered as Mahādhyāta.
According to his capacity, he recognizes the supreme Hari and always knows the qualities present in Rudra and the others.
Therefore, O best of birds, this is indeed declared to be the name Vijñāna;
and it is traditionally remembered as Virāga because of the renunciation of actions performed for the sake of desire.
Alternatively, that vital air (māruta), residing eternally in the hearts of yogins, generates dispassion; therefore, it is known as Virāga.
For the gods, happiness increases ever further due to their merit and demerit;
that happiness extends upward through the higher realms as far as the world of Vāyu.
Furthermore, because Vāyu produces a portion of happiness for the gods, the sages, and likewise for the most excellent of men, he is therefore designated as "Sukha" (Happiness).
O Lord, the wind is the primary element there that always consumes the vigor;
however, the gods experience some slight suffering, grief, and the like.
Know that this is due to the influence of the Asuras; of this there is no doubt.
That [power] may belong somewhat to the individual soul, and it shall gradually accrue to the Daityas.
Since Kali is predominant, he is remembered as being sorrowful;
due to the merit and demerit of the Daityas, their suffering increases further and further.
O Lord of the Twice-born, he always experiences that suffering and that of the subsequent ages up until the end of the Kali age;
therefore, it is known as Kali.
O Lord, if some degree of happiness, joy, or the like occurs among the Daityas, it must be due to the possession of a deity; there is no need for further deliberation on this point.
O son of Vinatā, there is no hell for the gods;
nor, O twice-born one, is there even that which arises from sense objects, for it is of the very nature of happiness for the Daityas.
Even that slight darkness arising from sense objects which is uttered due to possession by a deity does not exist for the gods at all; by their very nature, there is no suffering.
The great suffering arising from sense objects never exists for the gods;
nor does any suffering, grief, or the like ever occur to them due to possession by asuras.
Therefore, O Lord of Birds, Kali is always miserable, while Vāyu is always happy;
such is the happiness and suffering of both men and sages.
By virtue of that merit and demerit, Māruta shall be an enjoyer of merit;
there is no need for deliberation here regarding the destruction of suffering and the dissolution of the impurity.
O Lord of Birds, the nineteen parts, beginning with *prāṇa* and ending with *sukha*,
have entered into the worlds and exist there separately.
And hear now, O best of bird-lords, concerning the Marutas, the Revatas, and the Ārās;
among the fourteen moons, the second was Virocana.
O Lord of Birds, he is proclaimed as Vāyu among Indra and the other gods;
within all the elements of the color green, he whose gaze extends everywhere is diffused.
Therefore, that portion of the Maruts known as Rocana was proclaimed to be Hanumān in the incarnation of Rāma, who accomplished the purpose of Rāma’s mission;
he himself was born on earth as the exceedingly powerful Bhīmasena.
In the incarnation as Kṛṣṇa, he is to be known as the celebrated portion of Marut.
There will be a Daitya named Maṇimān who is well-known;
he will undoubtedly cause the intermingling of all [classes]. (GarP 3.16.70)
Therefore, O Lord of Birds, he shall be known by the name Saṃkara;
he will utterly destroy all the Bhāgavata doctrines in every way.
Then Vāsudeva will appear on earth; of this there is no doubt.
There is no one equal to him in the fourteen worlds for the purpose of performing sacrifices.
Therefore, he will undoubtedly become full of wisdom;
the doctrine known as Bhāgavata is considered to be the three incarnations of Vāyu.
Establishment and the subduing of the wicked—these two alone are the purposes;
there is no other purpose for the wind-element, nor likewise for that which consists of Vairocana.
O Lord of Sages, in the three descents [of the Buddha], there is no suffering arising from the womb and so forth;
indeed, it does not exist at all, nor does it exist for Vāyu, nor likewise for Vairocana and the others.
For in the four modes of descent, O Lord of Birds, there is no connection with semen and blood; indeed, it does not exist at all, and since that is absent, there is nothing impure.
Having first dried up the embryo at the time of Prabhava,
the Goddess of the Gods indeed manifests during the four incarnations.
O Lord of Birds, the twenty-three forms of Vāyu,
as well as the forms of Brahmā Parameṣṭhin, are of straight and upright nature.
This is indeed true, there is no doubt, regarding eternal bliss, happiness, and so forth;
one should understand it exactly thus, and not otherwise in any way whatsoever.
By merely hearing this, they attain liberation; of this there is no doubt.
O best of the lords of birds, listen as I describe those born immediately after that. GarP_3,16.80.
O Lord of Birds, when Pradyumna was born from Kṛtī, two twin girls were also born; between those two, however, was Yadyikā.
O Lord of Sages, they know her who is named Vāṇī as Brahmāṇī; she is considered Sāvitrī, the wife of Viriñca known as Puruṣa,
and she is celebrated as Sarasvatī, the wife of the Four-faced One.
Thus, O best of birds, the threefold nature of speech should be understood;
I shall now describe the incarnations of Bhāratī—listen with a concentrated mind.
Because she possesses the conceit of all the Vedas, she is remembered as being composed of all the Vedas;
she is proclaimed to be the wife of the great meditator Vāyu.
She is proclaimed to be the wife of Vāyu, who is of the nature of knowledge;
and because she is eternally of the nature of bliss, Bhāratī is essentially blissful.
She is proclaimed as the wife of Vāyu, whose nature is bliss;
Vāyu himself is said to be her guru, and she remains devoted to him with true piety.
Then there is the eternal Bhāratī, known as Gurubhakti;
she is indeed proclaimed to be the wife of the great guru Vāyu.
Because it contains oil (sneha), it is remembered as "Hariprīti" (the beloved of Hari);
she is also proclaimed to be the wife of Vāyu, whose form is fortitude (dhṛti).
Because she takes pride in all mantras, she is remembered as being of the nature of all mantras;
she is indeed proclaimed to be the wife of the great lord Vāyu.
All enjoyments are indeed enjoyed solely for the sake of pleasing Viṣṇu;
therefore, Bhāratī should be known as she who is celebrated by the name "Bhujin" (the Enjoyer).
She is proclaimed as the wife of Vāyu, who is of variegated form;
and she who is called Śraddhā is proclaimed as the wife of Indra.
And at that time, O best of birds, Hanumān was born during the Tretā age;
then, she who is known as Bhāratī was born from the brahmin named Śiva.
Not only was Bhāratī joined with Aśacī and the others,
but all those born from her attained union with their respective husbands.
And she should be known as Anyageti, the maiden named Tanmati;
at the end of the Tretā age, O Lord of Birds, she shall be united with Śacī and the others.
Because she was born from the fire for Damayantī, she is called Indrasenā;
and because she brings joy to Nala, she is also known as Nalanandinī.
In that case, O Lord of Birds, one does not attain union with one's own husband;
rather, it should be understood that there is union with another man due to the wind residing within the person.
Having remained in that state for some time, she died as a maiden;
she herself was then born to the high-souled Drupada along with Śacī and others.
Born from the center of the sacrificial altar specifically for the sake of Bhīmasena,
she has no connection whatsoever with others, nor is there any union with other husbands.
The daughter of the King of Kāśī should be known as the sole Bhāratī;
she is to be known by the name Kālī, the eternal beloved of Bhīmasena.
Draupadī, the daughter of Drupada, endowed with speech and all other faculties,
having cast off her body, entered [the body] known as that of Kāraṭī in the village of that name.
O Lord of the Gods, she will exist in the house of Saṃkara during the Kali age;
for the sake of the third form of Vāyu, that maiden has met her death.
O best of sages, O lord of birds, these wives of Vāyu and the wives of Brahmā were indeed inferior to their own husbands by a hundredfold in their qualities.
Thus ends the sixteenth chapter, titled "The Description of the Incarnation of Mahālakṣmī and Other Matters," in the Brahmakāṇḍa, the third part of the Uttarakhaṇḍa of the glorious Garuḍa Mahāpurāṇa.
Śrī Garuḍa Mahāpurāṇa—Chapter 17.
Garuḍa said:
"O Kṛṣṇa, it has been said that during four births, Bhāratī was indeed born on earth together with Śacī and the others, distinguished by a single body."
"O Brahmin of noble vows, tell me the reason for this, for I am your disciple.
Thus addressed by Garuḍa, Madhusūdana spoke to him.
Śrī Kṛṣṇa said:
O best of birds, O lord of birds, I shall tell you the reason for Bhāratī’s attainment of this distinguished body; listen with an attentive mind.
Long ago in the Kṛta-yuga, O Lord of Heroes, Pārvatī was the wife of Rudra;
Śacī-devī was the wife of Indra; and Śāmalā was the wife of Yama.
O bird, the goddess Uṣas, the wife of the Aśvins, together with her husbands, went to the world of Brahmā; there they then beheld Brahmā.
O best of birds, seeing them acting so insolently, Brahmā immediately displayed gestures, expressions, and amorous charms, and then cursed them.
"O Lord of Birds, because you were arrogant, you shall obtain human birth; there, you shall attain union with your own husbands."
Thus cursed, they all went to Mount Meru;
there they easily deceived Brahmā as he sat upon it.
O Lord of the Gods, while he remained silent, they stood there again, deceiving him; then, as he remained silent, O Lord of the Gods, they deceived him directly.
After three times [the attempt], the great lord Brahmā cursed them:
"Because you deceived me three times and showed yourself only once. (GarP 3.17.10)
Moreover, after not having heard this, later on in four births upon the earth, human status will be attained from a single body; of this there is no doubt.
In your second birth, you shall likewise attain another state of existence;
in your third birth, you shall likewise obtain union with a husband.
"In your first birth and in the fourth, you shall not attain the state of going to another [husband],
nor shall you ever obtain union with a husband other than your own."
O best of birds, having been thus cursed by Brahmā,
they all then gathered on the summit of Mount Meru and deliberated.
The curse of a Brahmin cannot be extinguished even by hundreds of means; likewise, association with the base is censurable and brings about calamity.
Through the highest association, even with a divine being, one may become a giver of wealth;
Vāyu is the supreme among the gods, so one should cultivate association for his sake.
Having reflected thus, Umā and the others performed service to Bhāratī;
at the end of a thousand years, that Bhāratī, being pleased, spoke:
"And for what purpose indeed will those of virtuous vows practice service to me? And how will those goddesses, devoted to her, express their own intentions? Thus they spoke. (GarP 3.17.18)
"Formerly, O beautiful women, we were cursed by Brahmā in his wrathful form: 'You shall attain human status from a single body.'"
"O Lord, even in your fourth birth, and likewise in your second birth,
you shall attain another state"— thus was she cursed, O beautiful lady.
"O Goddess, it was not our fault that we were led astray by the god Vāyu;
therefore, O Goddess, we desire to share one body with you throughout all our births."
Then, O best of the twice-born, having been thus addressed by them and having replied "So be it," that Bhāratī,
joined by Pārvatī and the others, became manifest on earth.
In the house of the brahmin named Śiva, that maiden performed austerities for the sake of unifying her practice with Viṣṇu, who is known as Śiva.
O women, at this third birth as Kṛṣṇa, the great lord Viṣṇu, known as Śiva, being gratified by their ascetic penance, granted them a boon.
There will be a union with the husband who is Righteousness (Samyaktva), even without worldly existence;
for she, Pārvatī, has been impelled in every way by him.
She displayed the splendor of the supreme Brahmā;
therefore, Pārvatī is the most excellent within the body of Brahmā, without a doubt.
Even with a dark body, she will have no union with him;
in this second [birth], she will become another woman—of this there is no doubt.
Hari, the Lord, who was stationed within Rudra, having bestowed his seed upon the woman, vanished;
the glorious one departed for his own world.
Having cast off that body, they became the daughters of Nala;
having received the name Indrasenā, they went to the forest of asceticism.
As they were wandering there, they saw the sage Mudgala;
by the mere sight of him, they became infatuated with desire.
Having destroyed Mudgala’s pride, the Wind-god delighted the excellent women there, such as Bhāratī and others.
Emanated from that body, she became known as Draupadī;
because she was born from Drupada, she is remembered as Draupadī.
Since she emerged from the center of the sacrificial altar, she is remembered as being born from a womb;
and because she was black in color, she is known on earth as Kṛṣṇā.
The pride of Bhāratī is always remembered as belonging even to Kṛṣṇa’s body; however, the pride of Śacī and others belongs to that body only at certain times.
O best of birds, it is only for her who possesses such pride at the time of union with her own husband that this occurs, and not otherwise.
O best of birds, at the time for these women's dalliance, Umā has no pride at all; she is always delighted by sleep alone. (GarP 3.17.36)
It is recorded that at the time of Pārtha’s delight and during the physical presence of Draupadī,
there were two distinct forms of self-identification belonging respectively to Bhāratī and Śacī.
At that time, there shall be a destruction of the pride of Umā and others, as well as Śyāmā and the rest;
all of them shall indeed fall asleep—no doubt should be entertained in this matter.
Vāyu himself entered Arjuna in the form of a hero,
while Yudhiṣṭhira constantly delights in Bhāratī and Śāmalā.
O bird, having entered Nakula with his beautiful form like the wind,
he always delights in the daughter of Bhārata, while Nakula also delights in Uṣā.
And the Marut entered Sahadeva in the form of Nīti;
O bird, he constantly took delight with Draupadī, who was devoted to Sahadeva. (GarP 3.17.41)
Śacī and the other goddesses did not attain union with the body of Draupadī, nor did Māruta;
therefore, one should not imagine that their transference to another body applies to the body of Kṛṣṇā.
One should not at all contemplate union with the bodies of Dharma and the others, nor with Bhāratī;
rather, one should contemplate union with those [goddesses] in the form of a human body.
But for those women who possess direct perception [of the truth], there is no application of ointment whatsoever;
or else, O Lord of Birds, it is like that of Mudgala at the time of sexual union.
Thus they both took their pleasure; therefore, O Lord of the Gods, no fault is found in them. On that same day, both Dharma and Vāyu [did likewise]. (GarP 3.17.45)
O giver of honor, they both engaged in perfect dalliance even within the body of Kṛṣṇa;
nevertheless, there is no doubt that her state of being devoted to no other must be contemplated.
The deities know the enjoyments that are fit for the gods to enjoy;
however, they do not know at all those mortals who are within those very bodies.
Only the swan, and no other, knows how to distinguish milk from water;
therefore, O Lord of Birds, one should contemplate union with one's own lord through the body of Kṛṣṇa, and one must never contemplate the body of Kṛṣṇa as being separate [from him].

Thus ends the seventeenth chapter, titled "The Description of the Cause for the Attainment of a Distinguished Body by Bhāratī," in the Brahma-kāṇḍa, the third part of the Uttara-khaṇḍa of the glorious Garuḍa Mahāpurāṇa.
In the glorious Garuḍa Mahāpurāṇa— Chapter 18—
Śrī Kṛṣṇa said:
Now, O best of the lords of birds, I shall speak of those born immediately after;
listen with attention and, having heard them, retain them in your mind. (GarP 3.18.1)
The immensely powerful Śeṣa was born as the younger brother of Viriñca, who is known as Puruṣa;
he is the one upon whom Hari and Ramā rest while they sleep within him.
This was for the purpose of providing a bed; it was not for any purpose of Hari’s own. "I am always a servant of Hari; I am always a worshiper of Hari. (GarP 3.18.3)
"O Hari, I always bow to you in birth after birth.
Having been thus awakened, Garuḍa indeed became the couch for Hari.
O son of Vinatā, this son of Vāyu, named Kāla, was always known by the name Sūtra,
and he became Garuḍa for the purpose of being Hari’s vehicle.
Then, O Lord of Birds, from Viriñca, whose body is the principle of Mahat,
I was born as Rudra, consisting of the ego-sense (ahaṃkāra), in order to protect Hari.
O highly fortunate one, these three are remembered as being equal to one another;
yet those three are a hundred times superior to both the Gāyatrī and the Bhāratī.
He alone should be known as the remainder, the devotee of Nārāyaṇa,
Viṣṇu, Vāyu, and Ananta, who is always endowed with three portions.
O bird, that Lakṣmaṇa who was born from Daśaratha as a portion of Sumitrā should also be known as Śeṣa, endowed with portions of Vāyu and Ananta.
O Lord of Birds, that Sītā was born from the Earth to perform service for Rāma;
and Balabhadra was born from Vasudeva and Rohiṇī, O Bird.
But this very one, the son of Rohiṇī, should be known as being endowed with two portions; he was entered by Hari during both the bright and the dark fortnights.
These three illustrious incarnations of the serpent are recorded;
there is no incarnation of the Lord of Serpents on earth, nor likewise the command of Hari.
I shall now describe the incarnations of Rudra; listen to them with a concentrated mind, O Lord of Birds.
He who is Rudra, whose nature is the principle of ego (ahaṅkāra), became that very [incarnation], O Khageśvara.
That destroyer obtained the name Sadāśiva;
he should be known as the one who presides over darkness (tamas), and because of his non-Śiva nature, he is called Sadāśiva.
Since he always wears an inauspicious garland of skulls,
he should be known as a Sadāśaiva, and not Śiva who is a Bhāgavata.
Since Hara wears the elephant hide as his sacred thread,
Hara always removes all inauspicious things from the worlds.
Because he always turns away from worldly objects those whose minds are attached to them by the command of Hari, he is therefore called Sadāśiva. (GarP 3.18.17)
Sometimes, due to the influence of the asuras, Hara acts contrarily;
therefore, he should be known as Sadāśiva, but not as Śiva, the devotee of the Lord (Bhāgavata).
Since this Hara desired to dwell in a cremation ground,
he should be known as Sadāśiva, and not as Śiva the devotee of the Lord (Bhāgavata).
O best of birds, Rudra entered the salt waters to perform penance for ten years; therefore, he acquired the name Tapas.
Śuka, the son of Vyāsa, is said to have been endowed with the descent (āveśa) of Vāyu;
he should be known as an incarnation of Rudra who appeared on earth for the sake of knowledge.
From Anasūyā, the wife of Atri, was born Rudra of great ascetic power;
he is to be known as Durvāsas, for the purpose of breaking the pride of kings.
Born from Droṇa and known as Drauṇi, he is proclaimed to be Rudra himself;
desiring to experience his *prārabdha* karma, he manifests as the adversary.
Rudra, who is stationed in the northeast corner and indeed attained the name Vāmadeva,
is always served by Vāyu, who stands on his own left side as a worthy devotee.
Therefore, Rudra obtained the names Vāmadeva, as well as the status of being disciplined and supreme;
he attained the nature of Time and the nature of Power, but not because of physical beauty.
The great-souled Rudra, desiring to slay the Daityas dwelling in Tripura who were enemies of Viṣṇu, assumed a non-terrible form;
therefore, Rudra himself received the name "Aghora."
To those hosts of Daityas who desired to perform service and were undergoing affliction through austerity for some time, he was immediately born to grant boons; thus he obtained the name Sadyojāta.
The son of Uru was Aurva, who is proclaimed to be Rudra himself; because he causes weeping (*rudana*) without being dragged (*akṛṣṭa*), he is called "Rudra. (GarP 3.18.28)
For this reason, Rudra was called "Uru" (the Wide), and his son was named Aurva;
in order to leave Rudra as the remainder, Aurva became Rudra himself.
Garuḍa said:
O Hari, why does Hara, who is known as Uru, weep?
And why does he, who takes the form of Aurva, weep with his chest left bare?
"O you of noble vows, explain this in detail to me, your grandson.
Thus addressed by him, that Hari, the ocean of compassion, spoke.
Śrī Kṛṣṇa said:

Having beheld his own form named Saṃkarṣaṇa, which is complete with excellent qualities, whose lotus feet are bowed to by Śrī, Brahmā, Śeṣa, Jiṣṇu, Kāma, as well as others, and by Bhāratī and Svastimat eternally; GarP_3,18.32 //

Upon seeing Hari, Rudra’s body was covered in horripilation; his eyes filled with tears, his throat choked, and he was filled with joy—joy that he had never before experienced throughout all the beginningless and endless cycles of Brahmā.
"O Lord, by what merit was my lotus-foot, adorned with beautiful anklets, seen by me?
Having seen and then not seeing the lotus-foot of Murāri again and again, my throat became choked. (GarP 3.18.34)
Rudra wept, his limbs trembling with fear: "O Lord, how shall I see you again?
O Mukunda, Nārāyaṇa, Universal Form, how shall my faculty of speech perform your praise? (GarP 3.18.35)
My vision is always associated with sin, and likewise my speech is always associated with sin;
my vision has always been attached to women, whereas your vision of me is indeed unattached.
O Viṣṇu, there is no capacity for you to properly praise those things to which one is attached, such as sons and wives;
there is no room for speech in the praise of Viṣṇu. By what merit, O Lord, have I been seen by you?
O Lord Anantakarṇeśa, known as Sucandra, you have never heard my discourse with your ears;
yet I have heard many worldly rumors. By what merit, O God, have I beheld you?
Having looked at the footstool of Hari again and again, Kaṭha became obstructed;
Rudra wept with his limbs trembling from fear, wondering how he might ever hear the story again.

O Lord Vaikuṇṭha, you are known as the excellent wind; and that which is offered to you, such as perfumes and flowers, is never smeared by those who handle it, nor is it defiled by the mud and water of urine, feces, and the like.

O Mukunda, by what merit have I been beheld by you, O Lord—with the water from the breasts of women, the water from their hair, the water from their armpits, the water from their limbs, and with unoffered garments, perfumes, and so forth? (GarP 3.18.41)
Having smelled the fragrance of the Lord’s floral remains again and again, Rudra’s throat became choked;
with his limbs trembling from fear, he wept, wondering how he might ever touch them once more.
O Nṛsiṃha, O Lord of the Nose residing in the nose, by my nose the fragrance of a beautiful lotus has never been smelled anywhere;
yet thus it is smelled again and again, as are unoffered perfumes, flowers, and the like.
"O Lord, Murāri, by what merit was Your face—with its beautiful nose and excellent teeth—beheld?
Having smelled again and again the fragrance of Viṣṇu’s remains, his throat became choked. (GarP 3.18.44)
Rudra wept, his limbs trembling with fear: "How do I smell this *nirmālya* of yours?
O Murāri, you who possess consciousness, it has been placed even upon your tongue by the faculty of the tongue."

He who daily bathes in front of Murāri with the remnants of the food offering mixed with *tulasī*, and especially sprinkled with the water from [the Lord’s] feet, obtains the merit of ten million times ten million sacrifices.
O Mukunda, such remnants of your food offering—which are indeed the form of the Sun himself—I have eaten many times without first offering them to you, the Lord Viṣṇu. (GarP 3.18.47)
O Lord, by what merit was it seen by me that edible and consumable food was not offered at Your lotus feet?
Having repeatedly enjoyed the various offerings made to Hari, I experienced Your bliss, cherished by Ramā.
They say your head, adorned with a crown and curly locks, rests upon heaven and earth;
yet it has been seen by me through the accumulation of merit earned over many births and through association with the virtuous.
"O God of gods, due to the accumulation of sins earned over many lifetimes, he will become invisible.
Thus Rudra wept with great devotion upon seeing Hari, who is complete in all auspicious qualities.
"O Viśvamūrti, O Vāsudeva, your lotus-foot is held within the hearts of the lords of yogis; it was seen by me through your compassion. How shall I see it again? Thus he wept.
"O Lord, I have seen the enemy's army filled with conchs, discs, and other weapons that destroy existence, as well as the three worlds themselves;
yet how shall I ever behold such a belly of yours again and again, O Rameśa? Thus he wept.
O Lord, may your broad chest— filled with bliss, filled with nails, filled with beautiful hair, filled with body-hair and other qualities,
and filled with a lovely neck— be adorned with true ornaments and graced by the stainless Kaustubha gem along with Lakṣmī.
I have beheld your chest with eyes of compassion— so very tender, adorned with blossoming *tulasī*, and likewise anointed with sandalwood paste.
"How might I see him again and again? Thus Rudra wept with devotion;
therefore, having obtained the name Tūru, that very Rudra became his son known as Daurvāsasa.
Because he made Rudra weep (rudam) and left him behind (urvitam), he therefore became known by the name Aurva.
And Aurva, seeing that the worlds were fit for liberation yet remained utterly addicted to sense objects, [acted accordingly].
And Śukra, repeatedly remembering the lotus-foot of Viṣṇu, became choked with emotion;
while those most wicked ones, day by day, indulged in sinful forms and evil objects through their corrupt senses.
"When shall I abandon these with the thought that they are to be discarded? I do not know," he wept thus truly;
for these fools exert themselves with the utmost diligence to acquire sense-objects for the sake of profit.
For all those who are devoted to sense objects abandon even their wealth and other possessions for the sake of a mere trifle;
O You whose form is the universe, when will You release these people whose intellects are destroyed and who are deluded by Your māyā?
Remembering again and again the illusory power of Vāsudeva, Atri wept, his limbs trembling with fear;
abandoning his own duty and resorting to a state of wretchedness through the most painful worldly conduct, he lamented. (GarP 3.18.60)
Having acquired wealth and such with extreme wretchedness, all those of very sinful character squander their hard-earned money and possessions in vain, like mere beasts.
"Out of the illusory power of Murāri, they never abandon those who have become worthy recipients, regarding them with the same mind as Viṣṇu himself.
The great ones say that the lives of those who ask 'How have they been lost? are in vain. Thus he wept properly.

O Kṛṣṇa, O Viṣṇu, seeing that their lifespan has thus passed in vain and their youth is indeed certain [to end], Death laughs as it rests upon their shoulders; yet those of deluded minds do not perceive this.
May my house endure for a hundred years; may my sons likewise live for a hundred years;
and may I live happily for a hundred years, as does my wife of auspicious marks.
I possess cows filled with excellent milk, and my friends are indeed endowed with joy;
I shall give a son for the purpose of protection, and I give my daughter to the bridegroom for the sake of marriage.
"I shall give my daughter to the virtuous, and I shall always give wealth to the wealthy;
yet the Blessed Lord Vāsudeva, seeing those who have never seen the Void, laughs at them constantly."
"I shall not listen to the discourse, thinking 'there will be the destruction of my fortune';
nor shall I ever worship Hari, thinking 'there will be the destruction of my sons and others.'"
"From time to time, Hari, known by various names, is the bestower of fruits for everyone—Vāsudeva, the source of all.
Seeing such foolish people, Akrūra, who was solely devoted to Vāsudeva, wept.
Therefore, O Lord of Birds, know that Aurva is eternally Rudra in form, his purpose well-instructed by Kṛṣṇa;
when Satī, the daughter of Dakṣa, O Lord of Birds, abandoned her own body at Dakṣa’s sacrifice.
Then Rudra was born again from Menakā to Himavat; he received the name Aurva, and having been told, "Become one whose seed is drawn up (ūrdhvaretas)," he indeed became Ūrdhvaretas.
When the high-souled Rudradeva took the hand of the daughter of the Himālaya mountain, he became utterly infatuated with her;
therefore, Rudra acquired the name "Para."

The ten Rudra-brothers beginning with Sadāśiva, the son of Sumitrā (Lakṣmaṇa), and the son of Hīḍimbā (Ghaṭotkaca)—these three are equal at the time of liberation and at the time of creation; yet they are inferior to those two [Rāma and Kṛṣṇa] by hundreds of qualities.
Garuḍa said:
O Kṛṣṇa, ocean of perfect compassion, please declare the definitive determination of bliss, so that it may be understood by me just as it is determined by the wise. (GarP 3.18.73)
Speak out of compassion for your disciple, so as to uplift me forever;
O Lord Kṛṣṇa, what desire can there be for you whose every wish is fulfilled?
Thus addressed by the high-souled Lord of Birds,
the lotus-eyed Kṛṣṇa, Hṛṣīkeśa, being pleased, spoke with compassion.
Śrī Kṛṣṇa said:
O Śatānanda, Ekānanda is the son of Vedhas; such a Śatānanda is proclaimed to be the son of Brahmā.
O best of birds, son of Vinatā, Śatānanda is known as the incarnation of Sarasvatī from Śeṣa and others,
while Ekānanda is to be understood as the incarnation of Bhāratī.
O Bird, such is the definitive conclusion regarding bliss that should always be known;
thus everything has been told by me—what else do you wish to hear?

Thus ends the eighteenth chapter, titled "The Description of the Gradations of Infinite Bliss and the Cause of Rudra’s Weeping," in the Brahma-kāṇḍa, the third part of the Uttara-khaṇḍa, in the glorious Garuḍa Mahāpurāṇa.
Śrī Garuḍa Mahāpurāṇa—Chapter 19.
Garuḍa said:
"O Kṛṣṇa, O Govinda, you have said that both Brahmāṇī and Bhāratī are superior even to Rudra by a hundredfold, O best of gods."
O Lord of the Gods, I have heard that Viriñca declared, even unto Umā, that [the world] was devoid of infinite portions. (GarP 3.19.2)
"O Kṛṣṇa, O Mādhava, O Lord Hari, you have stated that [the power] of all those ancestors is diminished by a thousandfold, having taken this into account."
O Maheśvara, from knowledge, bliss, power, and so forth, down to the vital breath itself, there is a deficiency of these qualities— knowledge and the rest— by a thousandfold part.
"O Govinda, speak a definitive conclusion; you are omniscient, there is no doubt.
Thus addressed by Garuḍa, Vāsudeva spoke with certainty.

Śrī Kṛṣṇa said: O Lord of Birds, it is clearly evident that for each successive stage among those mentioned above, this occurs precisely through yoga, with reference to its being devoid of portions of bliss.
When that bliss has increased a hundredfold in measure, due to its manifestation,
it is declared by Brahmā to possess infinite qualities.
And a thousandfold increase has been proclaimed by Vāyu regarding bliss; likewise, it applies to knowledge, devotion to Viṣṇu, and superior strength.
All these qualities have been described to you in their entirety, each increasing a hundredfold in succession;
the knowledge and bliss of Bhāratī are even greater, being increased by the power of devotion.
In this way, the knowledge of the power and other attributes of Māruta is easily understood;
thus, one hundred [such] knowledges are to be known regarding Māruta—of this there is no doubt.
The knowledge and power of Bhāratī are declared to be one hundred;
and likewise, the knowledge of Vāyu is clearly stated to be the same.
Just as a flame of fire, even if a hundred times greater than a lamp, is not like the lamp;
and just as fire, however abundant it may be, does not become like the sun. GarP_3.19.12.
Just as the moon, though twice the size of the sun, does not appear clearly,
so too has the gradation of bliss been described by me to you.
Know it to be exactly so, O bird, and not otherwise in any way;
I perceive the qualities residing within me, endowed with all their specific distinctions, O lord of birds.
O Lord of Birds, there is nothing whatsoever that exists which has not been seen by me, even in its most subtle forms.
Even in all his incarnations, the goddess Ramā knows Hari to be present.
That goddess understands all the qualities of Hari, endowed with every distinction and existing in an indivisible form;
that goddess understands them in their most subtle forms, and by my grace, she knows more than even Brahmā and the other gods.
The Goddess thoroughly knows her own essential nature, which is extremely subtle and endowed with excellent distinctions;
likewise, Lakṣmī thoroughly knows her own manifold expansion, which is also endowed with all its excellent distinctions.
Even Brahmā perceives Vāsudeva as all-pervading and His excellent qualities as superior to those of air and the other elements;
yet the sense of hearing does not know the qualities of Hari, which are extremely subtle in form and endowed with specific distinctions.
Just as the gods know [the Self] in its manifest form, so too do they not know it when it is unmanifest—except for Brahmā;
and both Brahmā and Vāyu always perceive themselves and other things as endowed with distinction.
Speech knows the qualities of Hari, yet even the Self-born Brahmā does not know His specific distinctions;
O Lord of Birds, one should always behold Viṣṇu in the form of Kṛṣṇa as eternally beyond the nature of the three guṇas.
Śeṣa, Rudra, and Vīndra—all these perceive the state established in mere darkness;
they know the qualities as perceived by speech along with their distinctions, but not the Truth itself, my dear friend. Thus has it been truly spoken.
Umā, Suparṇā, and Vāruṇī—these three together recognize him as well-established;
yet they do not know these specific attributes of Hari seen by Rudra, O Lord of Birds, in any place or time.
Indra and the others truly recognize Hari, whose pervasive form resides within the ego (ahaṅkāra);
and Dakṣa and the rest, as well as Soma, Sūrya, and others, know Him who is situated in the principle of intellect (buddhitattva).

O Lord of Birds, those who always recognize Viṣṇu as Hari, established in the true nature of all beings, and others who perceive him according to their own capacity as the form of Hari residing within the cosmic egg— GarP_3,19.25.
Some perceive the form of Hari residing within your heart, while others perceive it always within their own hearts;
know this to be the manner of things, O Lord of Birds, and now hear from me that these six are my wives.
O Lord of Birds, my six queens beginning with Rukmiṇī, as well as my wife Śrī and Nīlā—
who was the daughter of Havyavāhana in a previous creation— I worship them all immediately and without distinction.
O King of Birds, that maiden, the wife of Kṛṣṇa, would enjoy whatever desires she mentally conceived;
indeed, Kavyavāha alone always exerted extreme effort on behalf of her ancestors.
In that very same way, she did not obtain a husband, because her mind was focused one-pointedly on Kṛṣṇa.

Then Kavyavaha said to his son, "O dull-witted one, why do you not desire Hari as your husband? Then the daughter said to Kavyavaha, "O God, in this birth there can be no other husband for me, endowed as he is with all virtues; for Hari alone is the husband."
Therefore, all women in the world should always be known as widows;
for they are eternally without a beginning, the singular essence of the universe, most beautiful, and the bestower of liberation and the fulfillment of desires.
All those women who do not recognize such a one as this are indeed widows for all time—
those who fail to perceive the husband's form as the manifest sign of the soul, which is sustained by destiny yet deprived of devotion to Hari.

O dear one, there is no purpose in looking at this body— which is full of impurity, flowing from the nine apertures, endowed with a foul odor, and always loathsome— if one can abandon this dark [complexion] while the husband still lives.
The celestial women, having abandoned their own husbands, constantly delight in him who resides there;
therefore, they are always considered married and are to be venerated by all people—of this there is no doubt. (GarP 3.19.34)
If the husbands of these women were devotees of Hari, then the birth of these women would indeed be fruitful;
through the accumulation of merit earned over many lifetimes, their husbands may become devotees of Hari.
If their husbands are not devotees of Hari, they must certainly abandon their own bodies;
for if they should properly cast off their bodies while remembering their own husbands as Kṛṣṇa and Hari in form, [they attain liberation]. GarP_3,19.36.

At that time, indeed, there are no faults such as self-destruction for women; this is the conclusion established in the scripture. One should never associate with those women whose husbands do not know Viṣṇu. (GarP 3.19.37)
Through the accumulation of merit earned over many lifetimes, their husbands may become devotees of Viṣṇu;
for in the Kali age, devotees of Viṣṇu are rare, and devotion to Hari is always difficult to find.
In the world of mortals, the stories of Hari are difficult to find;
initiation into Hari is difficult to find, and indeed, the definitive realization of Hari’s true nature is difficult to find, as is association with the servants of Hari.
Circumambulation of Murāri is indeed difficult to obtain, and prostration to him is difficult to obtain in the Kali age;
likewise, the protection of his devotees is difficult to obtain, and the gift of food to true Vaiṣṇavas is indeed rare.

The worship prescribed in the Tantras is indeed difficult to obtain, and the utterance of the name of Murāri is difficult to obtain; the honoring of true Vaiṣṇavas is indeed difficult, and conversation with true Vaiṣṇavas is difficult as well. (GarP 3.19.41)
Touching a Śālagrāma stone is difficult to attain, and the sight of true Vaiṣṇavas is indeed difficult to attain;
touching a cow is difficult to attain in the mortal world, and a true singer and a true Guru are likewise difficult to find.
A virtuous wife and virtuous sons are indeed difficult to find; so too is the sight of Hari residing on Śeṣācala.
Even more difficult to obtain is the sight of Viṣṇupadī on the banks of the Kāverī at Raṅganātha.
In the sacred field of Kāñcī, service to Varadarāja and even the sight of him are extremely difficult to obtain in this world;
the sight of Rāmasetu is very difficult to obtain, and the capacity for the Madhva doctrine is likewise very difficult to attain.
The noble ones say that even for Viṣṇu stationed on the banks of the Bhīmā, a vision [of him] is very difficult to obtain;
and likewise for Viṣṇu stationed on the banks of the Revā, and for Viṣṇupāda in the sacred field of Gayā.
Likewise, even for Viṣṇu who is established on Badarī, it is extremely difficult to attain for those dwelling in the mortal world;
and ascetics such as Śeṣācala and Śrīnivāsāśrama are rare in the mortal world.
Indeed, even for Mādhava at the place called Prayāga, the constant vision [of the Lord] is difficult for men to attain.
"Therefore, I do not desire any husband other than Kṛṣṇa at any time.
Having spoken thus to her father, she departed toward Śeṣācala.
At the great sacred ford named Kapila, the great chaste lady ascended the great mountain; having seen Śrīnivāsa situated there, she bowed down to him.
Then, having fasted for three days and gone to Pāpavināśana,
he bathed there and proceeded to a secluded place for the sake of marriage.
Two *krośas* to the north of that place,
on a great plateau that had become a secluded hollow, he performed supreme austerity.
Having meditated upon the god Nārāyaṇa, the maiden remained there;
and at the end of a thousand divine years, she began to offer praise.
The maiden said:
You alone are my mother and you alone are my father; you alone are my husband and you alone are my friend.
You alone are my son and my most venerable teacher; you are my friend, my sister, and my beloved.

O Lord, even though we reflect upon it throughout beginningless and endless births, neither I nor all these others— such as my father and so forth— understand [the truth], for they exist merely as causal conditions, whereas You exist as the conditionless.
Therefore, O Lord of Murā, O you of generous form, my vow at that time was simply this: "May I become the wife of you alone;
for there is no perfection through union with those who are difficult to encounter and the like."
O God, best of servants, sever the sight of those who revile you;
O Viṣṇu, sever the sight of those who betray their gurus; O Kṛṣṇa, sever the friendship of those who betray your devotees.
O Lord, sever my speech with those words of malice; grant me union with Your lotus feet.
Salutations, salutations to You who dwell on Śrīśaila; salutations, salutations to You, the Abode of Śrī.
O Lord, O Rameśa, O source of all that is high and low, though a great deal of time has passed, you have appeared as a manifestation before me;
and through the means accumulated over infinite births, the vision of you, the Four-armed One, has been attained.
O Lord, how may I behold you, I who am thoroughly possessed of every fault, a slave of slaves, and a servant of your servants? Be gracious, O Lord of Gods, O Abode of the World!
Thus praised, Viṣṇu, the abode of Śrī, the ocean of compassion,
and Janārdana, the bestower of boons, appeared before her due to her devotion.
"Choose a boon; may it be well with you. I have come here as a granter of boons.
Hearing these words spoken by Hari, she, with a smiling face, replied: *GarP_3,19.61*
With supreme devotion, she spoke to Śrīnivāsa, the Lord of the universe:
"O Mādhava, O handsome one, may I indeed become your wife."
Having heard her words, Śrīnivāsa spoke these words;
the Blessed Lord said:
"O fortunate maiden, when Kṛṣṇa is born on the surface of the earth," GarP_3,19.63.
"I shall become your husband; there is no need for deliberation on this matter.
Thus was the maiden, the daughter, addressed by Hari, the supreme heap of merit.
Extremely delighted, she spoke with a voice faltering with joy. The maiden said:
"May I become the wife of Kṛṣṇa on the very first day of his birth."
"From my very first formation, I have chosen you from among the women.
When he had said "Om," Madhusūdana spoke these words again.
The Blessed One said:
"O beautiful lady, because they were chosen by the maiden and because of my granting [of the boon], the fulfillment of their heart's desire shall come to pass; of this there is no doubt."
Having thus granted her the boon, he vanished right there;
and the maiden, having cast off her body in that very place, became a daughter.
She was born in the house of Kumbhaka and is known by the name Nīlā;
O highly fortunate one, Kumbhaka was the brother-in-law of Nandaśobha.

He is to be known as Kalpavāha, remembered as the foremost of the ancestors (pitṛs). O best of birds, having gone to the home of that Śiva who dwells on Mount Vṛṣabha, I shall become invincible by his boon.
O Lord of Birds, having slain the sons of Diti, Nīlā arrived;
thereafter, she was born as a maiden in the house of King Agnijit.
Agni-jit did not become Kavyavāha; instead, he had a daughter named Nīlā.
At her svayaṃvara, I [presented] seven bulls.
"O great bird, having bound and conquered the kings who were like bulls—and who were indeed unslayable by gods or men due to the boon of Śiva—you have obtained Nīlā. (GarP 3.19.73)
Nīlā, the daughter of Kumbhaka, entered deeply into his body through a single limb; because she entered through that one part, she remained right there.
Born upon the earth in two ways, she is like a maiden; of this there is no doubt.
O best of birds, listen as I describe the auspicious birth. GarP_3,19.75.
Thus ends the nineteenth chapter, titled "The Determination of Nīla’s Marriage," in the Brahma-kāṇḍa, the third part of the Uttara-khaṇḍa of the glorious Garuḍa Mahāpurāṇa.
Śrī Kṛṣṇa said: [Chapter 20 of the Śrī Garuḍa Mahāpurāṇa] Śrī Kṛṣṇa said:
In a previous creation, she who was the daughter of Vīndra, named Nala, became the wife of Viṣṇu;
having performed a circumambulation with desire, she became Bhadrā, known by the name Bhadra, on account of her virtue.
Seeing her established in the state of maidenhood, her father Nala spoke to her who was known as Bhadrā:
"O Bhadrā, why do you cause pain to your body? O daughter, tell me the reason for it."
Bhadrā said:
"Listen to me, my dear; who indeed would be capable of describing the fruit of prostrations and other such acts?"
"Nevertheless, O dear one, I shall speak to you according to my ability; listen well for your own welfare.
Hari is always the compassionate Lord, and I am but a servant of His servants.
'Protect me! I bow at the feet of Viṣṇu, Your [Lord]'—having said this, he prostrated himself like a staff. (GarP 3.20.4)
The wise say that a prostration to Hari which is devoid of [proper] ritual action is useless; listen to this from me:
one should prostrate to the god Viṣṇu while saying, "O Lord of Ramā, O Lord of Madhu, O Lord of Sarasvatī."
O God of gods, just as you are pleased by salutation, you are not so satisfied by worship or ritual action;
nor can one restrain evil through other means as effectively as one does through the recollection of your name or your salutation.

But those, O dear one, who nourish only the body—which has become nourished while being empty of prostrations to Hari—say that such [nourishment] is indeed useless; they say that for those who nourish it in this way, there is suffering in hell.
Yama, too, having placed him there upon that mortar, grinds him with pestles;
or else, O dear one, he does not even perform a circumambulation of Viṣṇu, the God of gods.
Placing their very feet upon the foot-pressing machine, Yama constantly grinds them;
because they never utter the name "Hari-Kṛṣṇa," he declares their tongues to be eternally useless.
In the world of Yama, Yama constantly pulls out their tongues and grinds them;
O dear one, what purpose is there in residing at Kāśī, or what is the use of dying at Prayāga?
What happiness is there in dying at the front of an elephant, or what in the performance of sacrifices and the like?
What is gained by wandering to all the sacred fords, or by studying the scriptures with a very sharp intellect?
The great ones declare that for those on whose tip of the tongue the name of Hari does not reside, who do not bow with their limbs to Viṣṇu,
and who do not perform circumambulation of Hari with their feet— all of these things are in vain.
Why do they say that circumambulation and prostration performed while dedicating [the act] to Hari, as well as the offering of arghya, constitute worship?
Therefore, O dear one, prostration to Viṣṇu must certainly be performed, and the remembrance of Hari’s name must be practiced.
For this birth is difficult to obtain yet as perishable as something situated in water;
therefore, my dear, do not place your trust in your own body, nor even in your life, thinking "this is mine" or "that is another's."
Your bowing was performed this very moment, yet it was not truly yours; your remembrance was performed this very moment, yet it was not truly yours.
I do not know when I shall meet my death; therefore, O Great-Souled One, place no trust in this body.
Having heard these pure words of his daughter, Nala, O lord of heroes,
offered salutations and performed a circumambulation according to his ability.
She too performed circumambulations and prostrations to Hari constantly;
having done this for many days, she meditated upon the supreme Nārāyaṇa.
And at the time of death, O bird, he cast off his body while contemplating Hari within the womb of my father Vasudeva’s sister.
She was known by the name Kaikeyī, yet she was also called Bhadrā;
because she was endowed with auspicious qualities, she was named Bhadrā and bore that auspicious name.
O best of birds, he recovered this auspicious lady after she had been carried away by her five Kaikeya sons, O best of birds.
I shall tell you the reason for the marriage of Mitravindā;
listen with an attentive mind, O best of birds. (GarP 3.20.21)
Mitravindā said:
"In a previous creation, Mitravindā by name chose Agni and Soma not out of desire;
desiring to attain Hari as her friend, that goddess constantly reflected upon the means for that end."
The Goddess reflected upon which among those means for attaining Hari was the most principal;
she concluded that, even always, the hearing of Sāttvika Purāṇas is said to be the best among them.
Wherein the excellence of Viṣṇu exists, therein likewise exists the excellence of Vāyu and of virtuous people in the Purāṇa;
one should always perform the Śrāddha with the thought that it is for Viṣṇu, and no other means of practice should ever be proclaimed there.
They say that the birth of those on a day when there is no hearing of Viṣṇu’s narrative is in vain;
[so too are] their bathing, chanting, the five great sacrifices, religious observances, meritorious works and charities, penances such as the Kṛcchra and Cāndrāyaṇa, and whatever they have given.
All the initiation rites of the Vaiṣṇavas, even when properly performed,
are indeed in vain for those by whom the Bhāgavata Purāṇa has not been heard from gurus who are endowed with the traditional lineage.

The great ones say that the birth of those who have not heard the Bhāgavata Purāṇa and have not heard the ancient Brahmakāṇḍa is in vain; therefore, the discourse concerning Hari should always be heard.

One should not dwell even for a single moment, under any circumstances, in a place where there is no great river of the stories of Govinda, where there is no taking refuge at the feet of Nārāyaṇa, and where the name of Viṣṇu is never spoken.
In whatever village the scripture of the Bhāgavata does not exist, nor do those who know its rasa;
in whatever house there is no essence of the meaning of the Gītā; or in whatever village there is not the Thousand Names (Sahasranāma); [in such places, one should not dwell].
One should not dwell for even a moment, under any circumstances, where these three knowers of the essence do not exist;
for on whatever day there is no talk of the divine or of Viṣṇu, the life of that person is indeed in vain.
Once he has entered the womb, there is no need for further deliberation; that [birth] is considered difficult to obtain in the world of mortals.
Even an ear adorned with earrings for aeons, though beautiful, the noble connoisseurs of aesthetic flavor do not call truly beautiful.
The noble ones say that the ear is truly beautiful when adorned with the ornaments of stories concerning Viṣṇu;
therefore, those who constantly listen to and perpetually recite the essence of the meaning of the Bhāgavata [attain such beauty].
The great ones say that their birth is auspicious and that they likewise possess great fruit—
those mortals who always listen to or indeed recite the stories of Hari while wearing turbans and bodices.
Indeed, all those people in the world are worthy of honor who, being neither attached to their genitals nor to their bellies,
always speak of the Purāṇa— the essence of the Blessed One’s true reality— out of courtesy or out of desire for wealth.
But for those who conceal the secrets that must be hidden regarding the truth, their destination is always the son of the Sun (Yama);
they are those who constantly and perpetually take great delight in the section on dharma and the section on ritual action.
The destiny of those who recite the Purāṇa for a fee is always like that of a dog in the sun;
likewise, those who listen to the Bhāgavata Purāṇa for a fee do not truly grasp the essential meaning of Hari’s teachings.
The destiny of those who perform the study of the Vedas for a fee is always that of the Son of the Sun (Saturn);
however, those who are content with wealth obtained by chance are always fit for this [higher path].
Those who are possessed by excessive greed for the acquisition of wealth have no qualification whatsoever for the Bhāgavata [path].
Having realized that in this world Hari alone is eternally the inner controller, there is no other Lord besides Him.
Thus, for those who always contemplate in this way, Viṣṇu shall provide security and well-being.
For those true Vaiṣṇavas, there is no inauspiciousness; it is never seen, except as a form of doubtful knowledge.
Hari bestows the fruit of both auspicious and inauspicious deeds according to one's karma;
therefore, one should not exert effort for the sake of that [worldly fruit], but rather for the sake of wealth and indeed for the true nature of Hari.
Therefore, having bathed, recited the divine mantra, and offered the fragrance from Viṣṇu’s remains (nirmālya),
one should become pure and constantly cause the Bhāgavata Purāṇa to be heard, even if one is already all-knowing.
According to their karma, there shall be the acquisition of wealth, the acquisition of the Vedas, and the thorough study of the scriptures;
and there shall also be the hearing of Viṣṇu, yet hearing [of Him] with great reverence is difficult to achieve.
Out of great reverence, one should taste the essence of the Bhāgavata, which is difficult to encounter in the mortal world;
and having tasted that Bhāgavata Purāṇa, it is likewise difficult for one to be filled with tears of bliss.
The Noble Ones have declared that hearing the determination of the principles and retaining them all is extremely difficult;
and having heard the principles, it is difficult to retain them and subsequently to dissolve desire and anger.
Having heard that crossing over by means of the retention of the principles, as well as that which is difficult to accomplish and yet perfectly integrated in yoga; // GarP_3,20.45 //

Having heard the principles and immediately thereafter having mastered them, even the digestion of desire and anger—which is difficult to achieve—these defects always render even those purified by knowledge full of doubt in this world. (GarP 3.20.46)
Therefore, I shall always listen to the sacred discourse; there is no need for deliberation on this matter.
Having thus resolved my heart upon the desire for the name of Hari, I indeed applied myself to listening.
Having practiced such listening until the end of my body, I have been born here upon the earth after casting off that body.
O bird, you were to dwell in the womb of Vasudeva’s sister, named Sumitrā;
thus you were born as Mitravindikā.
By hearing [the name] of Hari as her friend, she attained Mitravindā;
therefore, she became known by the name Mitravindā.
O Lord of Birds, at the svayaṃvara, that beautiful woman placed the garland upon my shoulder amidst the kings; taking it,
O Lord of Birds, we shook off all the monarchs and reached the city.

Thus ends the twentieth chapter, titled "The Description of the Austerities and Other Deeds Performed by Bhadrā to Attain the Status of Being the Consort of the Blessed Lord," in the Brahma-kāṇḍa, the third part of the Uttara-khaṇḍa of the glorious Garuḍa Mahāpurāṇa. Śrī Kṛṣṇa said:
O Lord of Birds, I shall also describe the origin of Kālindī:
the Sun-god named Vivasvat begot her as his daughter.
O Lord of Sages, she who is known as Kālindī and remembered as the younger sister of Yama performed supreme austerity out of a desire to become the wife of Kṛṣṇa.
Austerity is said to be self-examination and the definitive discernment of the principles;
the remorse for sins previously accumulated is remembered as austerity.
"Prāya" is said to be austerity (tapas), and "citta" is said to be the restraint of the mind;
it is called "prāyaścitta," O Lord of Birds, and not the shaving of the head."
O Lord of Birds, listen to this true account joined with remorse:
O Mukunda, in the past the divine mantra was not recited by me, as I was constantly scorched by the forest fire of afflictions.
Indeed, the nectar of Hari’s name was not remembered, while the faults and such of Hari were constantly remembered;
the nectar of Hari’s true nature was not remembered, while idle gossip and the like were properly heard.
The lotus-feet of Hari were not worshipped, though sons, friends, and others were well-honored;
the lotus-feet of Hari were not saluted, though the feet of a most cruel friend were well-saluted.

O Mukunda, O Murāri, your face—endowed with the smoke of incense and covered by locks of hair—has indeed never been seen; yet while children and others were cherished, your own face was not cherished.
My son and friend were cherished with ornaments, yet that which removes all sins was not cherished;
indeed, the remainder of food offered to Hari was never eaten, yet food of the six flavors was eaten at the house of my friend.
O Murāri, those excellent flowers and perfumes were not offered by you to me; rather, they were offered to your sons, friends, and others.
I am tormented by my sons, friends, and the like; O Mukunda, when shall I behold your face?

O Mukunda, when shall I behold Your face, for my tongue has been scorched by the food of non-Vaiṣṇavas, by vegetables such as *śigru*, by food not offered [to You], by that which is improperly prepared, and likewise by things unfit to be eaten?

O Murāri, my body has never been purified by the worship of the eight-syllable mantra, nor by the divine holy waters of Viṣṇu, nor by the conch-water sanctified in the past; O Mukunda, when shall I behold your face?
O Mukunda, when will I ever purify my body—which has been scorched by the foul odors and defects of non-Vaiṣṇavas—with unoffered perfumes, flowers, ornaments, and various garments? GarP_3,21.13
My feet have been burnt, O Vāsudeva, and they do not go upon the path to the field of Hari;
my eyes too have always been burnt, O Lord, so that I have never beheld your form.
My hands are burnt, O Vāsudeva, for I have not worshipped the image of Viṣṇu. O Murāri, I have committed a multitude of sins; O Mukunda, when shall I behold your face?
O Mukunda, do not take full account of my faults; out of pure servitude, show me compassion.
O Lord, you who are far removed from all defects, there are as many hairs upon my body as there are [faults]. (GarP 3.21.16)
O Mukunda, when shall I behold your face upon my body, which has become as vast as yours, filled with sins,
and burdened by a wife, sons, a home, friends, wealth, cattle, servants, and the like?
Indeed, no happiness has been attained that is not equal to service to you, the divine Viṣṇu, O Mukunda;
beyond this, I shall leave behind son, friends, and the like, for I shall become your maidservant.
Those who might say that perfect happiness arises in the mortal world through sons, friends, and so forth—I know that urine, feces, and the like always fall directly from their mouths. (GarP 3.21.19)
Whatever collection of wealth has been acquired through friends and others that has gone to waste or become defiled,
and whatever collection of wealth has been acquired by true Vaiṣṇavas— that shall always be the cause for attaining Hari.
O Mukunda, such indeed has this come to pass; enough, truly enough, of the suffering he has endured because of association with the wicked and the constant absence of association with the virtuous.
O Murāri, my body has always been scorched by association with the wicked, not joined with dispassion.
O Mukunda, I do not know what state I shall go to being such as this; protect me with compassion!
For such is repentance, O Lord of Birds, which is the true expiation, and not shaving the head or other rites;
for Kanyā, having performed repentance toward the Sun, contemplated the true essence of Hari.
Hari alone is the supreme among all, because he is eternally complete with all qualities;
and since the entire universe is born from him at the time of creation, Hari is therefore full of all qualities.
He who is the primordial *akāra* of the gods, from whom Brahmā and all others are not at all complete;
by virtue of Lakṣmī’s grace and long-accumulated merit, Viriñca was born endowed with full qualities according to his fitness.
Viriñca is not full of virtues like Lakṣmī; nor is Ramā full of virtues like Viṣṇu.
Bhāratī is not full like Vāyu, nor is Vāruṇī full like Śeṣa.
Indeed, Pārvatī is not equal in form to Rudra, nor are others ever so complete;
having reflected thus, she performed austerities on the bank of the Yamunā.
Then, O bird, I went with Pārtha to the bank of the Yamunā for the sake of hunting;
and seeing her there performing penance, I spoke then to my friend Pārtha.
"O Pārtha, go quickly to the maiden and ask her, 'For what reason do you perform penance here?
Having been addressed thus, he went to her side and, having asked this cause, [returned] very swiftly.
Having arrived, Phālguna told me the entire account regarding her in my presence;
then, at an auspicious moment, I duly performed the marriage ceremony with her there.
And because of her constant burning and my constant contemplation, I am forever serene and ever perfectly tranquil;
always delighting in full bliss through her, what further happiness could there be for me, O Lord of Birds? (GarP 3.21.31)
"O Lord of Heroes, I accepted the marriage for her sake out of compassion, and not for my own pleasure;
O Lord of Heroes, I shall likewise describe the beauty of Lakṣmaṇā and the reason for taking her hand."
Listen, I shall tell you that truth; for there is nothing to be hidden from a good disciple, nor anything to be hidden from a guru.

Thus ends the twenty-first chapter, titled "The Determination of the Cause for the Marriage of the Blessed One with Kālindī," in the Brahma-kāṇḍa, the third part of the Uttara-khaṇḍa of the glorious Garuḍa Mahāpurāṇa. Śrī Kṛṣṇa said:

O Lord of Birds, she who was Lakṣmaṇā in a previous birth, the daughter of Vahniveda, the knower of the Vedas— because she was endowed with auspicious marks (sulakṣaṇaiḥ), she became renowned as Sulakṣmaṇā.
Just as Lakṣmī is perfectly complete with her characteristics, and just as Hari is indeed perfectly complete with his characteristics;
just as Vāyu is likewise full of his characteristics, so too is that Gāyatrī perfectly complete with her characteristics.

Just as Rudra and the others are indeed complete with their characteristics, and likewise [the Goddess] is complete with the characteristics of Rudra and the rest; so too, by virtue of their qualities and according to the nature of reality, a name is chosen through some slight consideration of their correspondence.
Therefore, they all call him Lakṣmaṇa; O King of Birds, first hear those auspicious marks.
In Nārāyaṇa, the Lord of Ramā who is full of all qualities, there are thirty-two auspicious marks.
"O Lord of Birds, they truly exist; I shall describe them to you in due order. Having heard this from me, one attains eternal liberation.
That person who has seven feet, ninety-six finger-breadths in stature, four arms, and sharp teeth—"
The noble ones say that all this combined together constitutes the single characteristic of Hari Viṣṇu;
the noble ones also say that a second characteristic of him is a face that is smooth, round, and full in form.
O Indra among heroes, the noble ones declare that the third characteristic is when one's jaw is not protruding;
and the noble ones declare that the fourth characteristic is when one's teeth are indeed sharp and fine.
O Lord of Birds, the noble ones say that the presence of redness upon the lower lip is the fifth mark;
and O Lord of Birds, the noble ones declare that hands which are exceedingly red are the sixth mark.
The noble ones say that the seventh characteristic is that in which the nails are red and very beautiful;
O Lord of Men, the noble ones say that the eighth characteristic is that in which there is redness upon the cheek.
The noble ones say that the hand in which lines such as the conch and the discus appear is the ninth;
and whose chest is well-nourished, marked with three folds in the form of threads, and beautiful.
The noble ones say that having tall limbs is the tenth mark; they say that having a deep navel is the eleventh;
and that whose two thighs are indeed fleshy, the noble ones call that the twelfth mark.
The noble ones say that for whom the hips are long and broad, that is the thirteenth mark;
the noble ones say that for whom the testicles are well-situated above, that is the fourteenth mark.
Furthermore, O Lord of Birds, that which has a prominent mark on the penis is said to be the fifteenth;
the soles of the feet being very copper-colored—the noble ones call that characteristic the sixteenth.

The two ankles are low; they say the seventeenth is the form of the neck, and the eighteenth is said to be the lotus-eye, which is deep red; the nineteenth is the arm, and likewise the twentieth is the knee.
They say that a chest twenty-one units wide is "lion-shouldered"; they say twenty-two is [the measure for] the shoulders;
twenty-three they call "subtle-mouthed," and twenty-four is for those with very serene eyes.
O Lord of the Twice-born, they say that a short penis and softness are the characteristics of the twenty-fifth [tattva];
and they say the twenty-sixth consists of the feet being even, as are the hips, knees, thighs, and shanks.
The noble ones declare that having equal hands and equal ears constitutes the thirty-second mark;
indeed, the thirty-two marks belong to Mukunda, and the thirty-two marks belong to Ramā.
They say that even Brahmā possesses the thirty-two marks, and that this is indeed true of his consort Bhāratī as well;
likewise, there is doubt regarding the Wielder of the Discus (Viṣṇu) being equal [to them]. Thus, O Sadāmā, I speak—make a firm decision.
Indeed, Lakṣmī never fully reached the end of even a single characteristic of Viṣṇu;
therefore, those who know his characteristics always declare Hari to be endowed with infinite characteristics.
O Lord of Birds, Lakṣmī knows the characteristic of Vāyu’s form as being superior to her own;
yet Bhāratī, in comparison to her own characteristic, is superior even to Brahmā by hundreds of qualities.
Therefore, O Lord of Birds, do not ever maintain a mind of equality toward Viṣṇu and the others regarding their characteristics;
for they, beginning with Rudra, are said to be twenty-eight in number, yet they are indeed deficient in the characteristics of the eyebrows and eyes.
That which is considered "without characteristics" by him is indeed a "bad characteristic," and that should not be contemplated at all.
O Lord of Birds, the twenty-eight characteristics of Hara are certainly not to be contemplated like [the qualities of] Bhāratī.
Therefore, Hara always exists in the form of wrath due to the absence of those two; thus it has been truly said that this is so.
Consequently, O Lord of Birds, these two do not exist in Rudra; there is no excess whatsoever in his head or belly.
Lakṣmaṇā and the others were endowed with twenty-seven auspicious marks;
Vāruṇī and the others possessed twenty-six, and Candra was endowed with twenty-five.
Artha is endowed with twenty-four [qualities], while Āyus possesses twenty-two; Śacī is undoubtedly endowed with twenty-one characteristics.
Pravāha is joined with twenty, Yama with nineteen,
Pāśa with eighteen, and Anala is joined with seventeen.
Vaivasvata is joined with sixteen, Mitra with fifteen,
the Lord of Wealth (Kubera) with twenty-four, and Pāvaka with thirteen.
Gaṅgā is joined with twelve, Budha is endowed with eleven;
Śani is numbered at ten, and Puṣkara is joined with nine.
Then there were sixteen thousand wives, my beloveds,
as well as eight [classes of] mothers and seven [classes of] fathers.
The gods and Gandharvas are said to possess six [qualities], those immediately following them five;
the rulers of the earth are declared to have four, and others are endowed with three.
