O Brahmin, when there is a slight protuberance on the abdomen, shortness of the feet and ears, and an excess of hair on the crest, this pertains to the wife of Śiva.
In the Lakṣmaṇā [lineage], there are five defects, excluding the head and the ankles;
when the navel is excessive, there are eight defects together in the Ativāhika [lineage].
When there is an excess of the shanks, eight defects are always recorded for Śacī;
in this very same way, O Lord of Birds, the defects are to be inferred [for others] as well.
O Lord of Sages, one who is always heard to possess ill-omened marks becomes a knower of reality;
he has a large belly, a protruding navel, and fierce fangs as long as a plow-pole.
With eyes as deep as blind wells, with hanging ears, lips, and nose, with pendulous ankles and crooked feet, he has deformed nails and black teeth. (GarP 3.22.35)
He is described as having long shanks and a long neck, a single leg and a single nose,
with red whiskers, red body hair, and a distorted face.
Kali is known to resemble a scorched tree trunk, with a red back;
he is hairless on his body and hairless on his head, and has red cheeks and jaws. (GarP 3.22.37)
O bird, there is constant paleness on the forehead, on the left shoulder, and on the hand;
likewise, one has a cruel gaze, a gaze fixed on the feet, and a gurgling voice.
Excessive eating and excessive drinking [are signs of decline]; the breasts become like dry fruits;
new hair grows on the thighs, as well as on the back and the head. (GarP 3.22.39)
On the forehead, three [lines] are long, while two are declared to be equal;
that fish which is shaped like a serpent is said to be at its tail.
The fish described as being at the tip of the tongue is like a sandal;
the fish shaped like the penis is praised for the anus.
A fish shaped like a scorpion is praised for its feet,
and a fish shaped like a dog is indeed proclaimed for its mouth.
There should be many lines on the hand, and hair is said to be present on the nostrils;
furthermore, the thumb and the little finger should not be excessively long.
"O Lord of Birds, such ill-omens as these exist indeed many times over in the Kali age;
however, O Lord of Birds, many auspicious signs reside within me."
"O Lord, those thirty-two marks of Viṣṇu were spoken by Brahmā to you with an underlying intention directed specifically toward those such as Brahmā."
O best of beings, there is no contradiction between what was spoken by Brahmā and what has been spoken by me;
that very one described by me as having a conch-like neck is indeed Vyāsa.
I have stated that the red lips and the red palate are to be unified;
therefore, there is no contradiction at all, for it is perceived through such knowledge.
Those women such as Lakṣmaṇā and others who are endowed with twenty-seven auspicious marks; GarP_3,22.48 //
In her private parts, eyes, hands, breasts, and likewise in her abdomen,
she possesses five fewer marks than Bhāratī.
O Lord of Birds, it does not possess the characteristics of Rudra nor any others;
it is endowed with twenty-six characteristics and is indeed devoid of the six characteristics of Vāruṇī.
There is a slight excess at the ears, the belly, the mass of hair on the nose, the ankles, and the genitals;
O Lord of Birds, Indra is always joined with twenty-five [marks], yet he is deficient in seven in number of characteristics.

One who possesses twenty-four marks—on the hands, feet, abdomen, ears, penis, ankles, and the lower lip—and likewise eight marks on the nose and the wind (the breath), [is a great being]. GarP_3,22.52 //
Śacī was endowed with twenty-three auspicious marks at the navel, the ankles, the chin, the two feet, the shoulders, the two eyes, and the lower lip; yet she was likewise possessed of nine defects.

O best of birds, know this: there is a slight excess [of hair] on the vulva, the hair, the lower lip, the ear, the shanks, the cheek, the chest, the two ankles, and likewise on the upper lip. GarP_3,22.54.
The wind named Pravaha is endowed with twenty-two characteristics and ten defects;
likewise, in the thumb there is a slight excess, and the Sun possesses twenty-one defects.
Then, the fire is endowed with twenty characteristics and joined with twelve defects;
it may also be endowed with nineteen characteristics and joined with thirteen absences thereof.
O bird, Vaivasvata was endowed with eighteen marks, while he [Yama] was without those fourteen;
Mitra, however, was endowed with seventeen marks.
One joined with these fifteen [planets] along with Rāhu is undoubtedly afflicted;
one joined with those sixteen is undoubtedly a lord of wealth. There is no doubt in this matter.
He is proclaimed as being joined with those sixteen absences;
and he who is joined with fifteen of them is known as the eldest son of Agni.
One who is joined with these seventeen defects has no doubt [of this];
likewise, Gaṅgā herself is proclaimed to possess these fourteen.
Likewise, there is no doubt that she is joined with eighteen defects;
however, Budha alone is joined with thirteen of them.
There is no doubt that Saturn is joined with nineteen defects,
along with twenty defects and twelve characteristics.
Puṣkara is proclaimed to possess eleven characteristics,
and he is described as having twenty-one non-existent states.
O bird, those ancestors who possess ten characteristics and are endowed with twenty-three defects are long-lived; of this there is no doubt.
The most excellent among gods and gandharvas are said to be endowed with eight characteristics and possessed of twenty-four defects.
The Gandharvas, who resemble humans, are endowed with seven characteristics;
they are proclaimed to be possessed of twenty-five defects.
Kings are endowed with twenty-six qualities and free from twenty-six faults;
others are endowed with five, and some indeed with only four.
O best of birds, there are none who lack even three of these;
O lord of birds, whatever excellence of marks is seen in that man or in a king, [it is due to these].
They are not truly men, nor indeed are they lords of the earth; for none of them are ever truly supreme.
This applies to all—whether they be gods or daityas—as well, O Lord of Birds.
O Bird, they have been described in sequence by their characteristics and non-characteristics; there is no doubt that they are endowed with twenty-seven characteristics and non-characteristics.
Therefore, she should be known as possessing the [thirty-two] marks, for she does not lack the thirty-two marks;
growing up in her father’s house, O Lord of Birds, she always seeks to exalt her own family.
She said to her father: "Food and other provisions should always be given to friends and others who are engaged in constant pursuit, whether they are situated inside or elsewhere. (GarP 3.22.72)
The virtuous say that food, drink, and other offerings given to one who is ignorant are indeed in vain;
therefore, listen today with reverence to my constant description of Hari, who resides here and there.
The child Hari, Kṛṣṇa, in the form of a boy, constantly takes milk and the like, fresh butter, and ghee;
he likewise takes ornaments and all kinds of clothing—one should always give these for the satisfaction of Viṣṇu.
Hari, known as Keśava and Mukunda, eats the food, drink, and other offerings given by friends;
therefore, a householder should always give first, for he will become blessed, otherwise it is indeed in vain.
Knowing that Hari, called Mādhava, eternally accepts [the offering], one should give food and other gifts;
knowing this, Viṣṇu is eternally pleased by what is given, and not otherwise, for otherwise it is indeed in vain.
O Suparṇa, Hari Vāsudeva always dwells in the home and is eternally pleased by staying there;
knowing this, one should always adorn one's own house at all times with the forms of the elements.
The one named Govinda dwells among the Vṛṣṇis, and Vāsudeva dwells together with his sons;
Mukunda is with his friend, Aniruddha is with his maternal cousin, and Nārāyaṇa is always present with the best of the twice-born.
Viṣṇu, in the form of Hari, is always present in the cow-pen, while the one named Vāmana always resides in the horse;
Saṃkarṣaṇa is ever present among the Śūdra class, and Pradyumna always dwells among the Vaiśyas.
Janārdana is always present in the kṣatriya caste; Hari is eternally among the fishermen (dāśas).
Indeed, the one Hari known as Upendra always and forever resides upon the earth, O Suparṇa.

The wielder of the discus always dwells in the elephant; the one of universal form always dwells within the ant; the creator of beings eternally dwells in the dog, and indeed at all times even in the termite.
Hari is Trivikrama in the intermediate space, and Hari possesses infinite forms within every species;
for Hari, who is the Lord of all diverse forms, there is no color, no lineage, and no birth.
Knowing this, the goddess Lakṣmaṇā always delighted Hari with the worship she performed, constantly thinking, "May Hari be my husband."
Desiring the status of being Viṣṇu’s wife, she abandoned her body and was indeed born as the daughter of the king of the Madras;
and at her svayaṃvara, O Lord of Heroes, I pierced the target and surpassed the lords of kings for Lakṣmaṇā’s hand.
Having performed the marriage with Lakṣmaṇā and returned to the city, I delighted the queen;
likewise, I shall tell you the reason why I married Jāmbavatī as my wife.
Thus ends the twenty-second chapter, titled "The Description of the Cause for Lakṣmaṇā’s Marriage," in the Brahma-kāṇḍa, the third part of the Uttara-khaṇḍa, in the glorious Garuḍa Mahāpurāṇa.
In the glorious Garuḍa Mahāpurāṇa— Chapter 23—
Śrī Kṛṣṇa said:
In a previous creation, the daughter of Soma was my wife Jāmbavatī, who was dear to me;
among them, O Lord of Heroes, she was indeed superior, being deficient in only five qualities compared to Rudra and the others.
When the possession by Ramā is powerful, then Keśava alone is honored;
when, over time, that possession diminishes, the great ones say there is equality among them.
There is indeed always some degree of possession by Lakṣmī; therefore, there is a slight superiority over those [other goddesses].
Garuḍa said:
O Kṛṣṇa, among them, what kind of worship did Jāmbavatī perform?
Tell me that out of compassion, O Viśvamūrti; for what indeed was the reason for her superiority over the others?
Thus addressed by Garuḍa, the Blessed One, the son of Devakī,
spoke to the son of Vinatā in a voice as deep as a thundercloud.
Śrī Kṛṣṇa said:
She who was the daughter of Soma in a previous creation, though remaining in her father’s house,
that virtuous woman indeed made her own birth meaningful by serving Viṣṇu together with her father.
She constantly listened to the true Purāṇas and always performed prostrations at the feet of Viṣṇu;
performing the remembrance of Viṣṇu, the Savior, she also always performed circumambulations of him.
But that maiden, together with her father, became filled with world-weariness upon hearing [the teaching];
she renounced her hair, her friend, the elephant and other [possessions], priceless jewels, the house, and so forth.
For he considered all this to be perishable, dependent upon himself, and indeed fashioned by Hari;
and since his sons, friends, and so forth were given by Him alone, he felt no pain when they were taken away by Him.
This very day, Viṣṇu, the supreme compassionate one, has shown mercy toward me, though not fully;
for that maiden, along with her father, O Lord of Sages, has [merged] into the eternally pure Vāsudeva.
O Lord of the Twice-born, because that goddess had approached with perfect devotion and spontaneity, she did not conceive of any livelihood for herself;
rather, she acted as if she were merely the first manifestation of the primordial power (prathā).
She indeed made her wealth consist solely in the lotus-feet of Viṣṇu, which carry one across the ocean of suffering;
she properly employed her faculty of speech, O bird, always for the description of the qualities of Hari.
The Goddess performed the cleansing of Viṣṇu’s body with her hands during the sweeping of his house;
and she applied her ears to the arising of Hari’s noble stories, which are like nectar and lead to the path of liberation and other goals.
The eye is the wheel for beholding images and the like, removing the impurities accumulated since beginningless time;
the skin is likewise for touching true Vaiṣṇavas, as well as for contact with the remains of offerings (nirmālya), fragrances, and unguents. (GarP 3.23.14)
She directed her sense of smell toward the essence of Hari’s feet, which grants liberation from saṃsāra;
and her sense of taste toward the remnants of Hari’s food offerings, mixed with the auspicious *tulasī* and other ingredients.
The feet [of the devotees] move along the paths to the sacred fields of Hari; their heads bow in worship at the feet of Hṛṣīkeśa;
and with hearts and mouths full of the desire for service to Hari, they wander as the followers of the One of Excellent Renown.
He fixed his mind upon the form of the desireless one, and the organ of speech took up the act of praise;
thus, he constantly offered the entire collection of his activities at the feet of the Supreme Lord.
He went with his father for the purpose of visiting sacred pilgrimage sites (tīrthas) specifically to please Lord Hari;
first, having honored the brāhmaṇas who were devotees of Viṣṇu at home with garments, ornaments, and other gifts.
Afterwards, the goddess made a vow before Viṣṇu for the sake of a pilgrimage:
"O Mukunda, for as long as the pilgrimage lasts, I shall remain a perpetual celibate."
For as long as I shall perform this pilgrimage, may there be association with Vaiṣṇavas from whom gifts have been received;
may there be listening to the stories of Hari, and never physical contact with non-Vaiṣṇavas who are not followers of Mukunda.
O Mukunda, I shall never undertake a long journey with my friends, sons, or other loved ones;
O Mukunda, keep far away from the company of those who perform pilgrimages out of worldly desire.
"What fruit do the noble ones say belongs to those who undertake a pilgrimage while leaving Śālagrāma behind?
At the very time when the sight of sacred fords (tīrthas) occurs, one should place the Śālagrāma in front."
O Lord of Birds, the noble ones declare that if one performs a pilgrimage to sacred sites on foot, the fruit is complete;
however, if one undertakes a pilgrimage to sacred sites while wearing footwear or using protective sandals for the feet, they say that pilgrimage is deficient in its merit.
If one performs a pilgrimage while seated upon a vehicle or a horse, the merit is said to be reduced by half;
if on a vehicle such as a bull, it is said to be a quarter; and if eating the food of others, they say it is rendered fruitless.
For those great-souled ascetics who know the Vedas and eat the food of others, there is no fault at all in eating such food.
Having resolved with the utmost reverence, she set out for the purpose of a pilgrimage to sacred sites.
Having first bathed and discarded the fragrance of Hari’s remains, he indeed performed the ritual of listening [to the scriptures];
and having also taken his meal together with his father, he traveled one *krośa* on the following day.
There, having honored the twice-born with food and drink, the Goddess caused them to hear the truth during the night.
The noble ones declare that for those who thus constantly perform this pilgrimage, their journey shall be fruitful.
"O Lord of Birds, the great ones have said that a pilgrimage to sacred sites is useless without compassion;
O Lord of Birds, those who do not listen to the divine stories of Hari by day or by night while on the path to the sacred sites [attain nothing]."
Know that the journey of his horses and other mounts has indeed been in vain;
declare the fault of the horses and so forth, for by the sight of the Gaṅgā and others, there is the destruction of sin.
From the sight of Viṣṇu residing in a sacred field comes the destruction of sin; speak of the transgression even of a cat [in this regard].
From the worship of Viṣṇu residing in a sacred field comes the destruction of sin; speak of the transgression of those who perform such worship.
For those performing recitations and other rites, there is the destruction of sin; from the meditation on Viṣṇu, there is the immediate destruction of poverty.
They say that everything performed devoid of such focused contemplation is indeed entirely in vain.
Therefore, O lord of birds, having heard this sin-destroying narrative of Hari, one shall become a devotee of Viṣṇu;
and by seeing, repeatedly seeing, and remembering, repeatedly remembering the footprints marked by Hari, one shall become a devotee, O lord of birds.
O Indra among sages, that maiden also went with her father to behold Śrīnivāsa residing on Śeṣācala;
along the way, she meditated upon Hari, the Lord of Ramā.
When shall I behold the broad chest of Śrīnivāsa, adorned with the jewel Śrīvatsa?
When shall I behold the beautiful belly of Śrīnivāsa, marked by the three folds of skin?
When shall I behold the neck of Śrīnivāsa, which resembles a conch shell and is the refuge of Maharloka?
When shall I behold the navel of Śrīnivāsa, which is ever the support of the intermediate space (antarikṣa) and is perfectly full?
When indeed shall I behold the face of Murāri, which is the eternal refuge of Janaloka?
When shall I behold the head of Śrīnivāsa, the eternal refuge of the world of truth?
When shall I behold the waist of Śrīnivāsa, the eternal refuge of the earthly realm?
When shall I behold the broad sole of Śrīnivāsa’s foot, which is the eternal refuge of Sutala?
When shall I behold the very tender knee of Śrīnivāsa, which is the refuge of Vitala?
When shall I behold the shanks of Śrīnivāsa, which are forever the refuge of the netherworld?
And when shall I behold the soles of Hari’s feet, which are forever the refuge of the realm of Pātāla?
While reflecting thus on the path, the goddess beheld Lord Śeṣa upon Śeṣācala,
resplendent with his thousand hoods, amidst various trees, monkeys, and female monkeys.
"By virtue of the accumulation of merit acquired over infinite births, this supreme mountain has indeed been seen by me today.
Upon seeing it, her eyes clouded with teardrops, she immediately rose and bowed her head in salutation."
Having looked at his face, she should perform a bow; she should not perform a bow by turning her back toward him.
She too performed twelve prostrations, having placed the Śālagrāma stone before him.
Thus, O Parvata, the Vaiṣṇavas must perform their duties, while you, indeed, must act contrary to the Vaiṣṇavas.
Śrīnivāsa, who dwells within honey, resides eternally on the mountain and is worshipped by Ramā, Brahmā, and the other gods.

"I shall behold the most excellent and supreme abode of Śrī, and then indeed I shall ascend the mountain. Having spoken thus, she established her residence at the sacred ford named Kapila together with her father.
Right here dwells Śrīnivāsa, Hari himself, neither by means of material substance nor in any other form.
Having first bathed there and performed the tonsure, one should cause the Tīrtha-śrāddha to be performed at that excellent sacred site.
Then, having given away all her possessions such as cattle, land, and gold, that virtuous woman ascended the mountain;
and he, having established the Śālagrāma stone before him, she too prostrated with great devotion.
Having thus ascended as far as the hundredth step, she sat down there;
she listened to the Bhāgavata Purāṇa and heard the praises of the Veṅkaṭa mountain.
From his preceptor Jaigīṣavya, he heard with great devotion the entire truth concerning the mountain of Veṅkaṭādri.
Thus ends the twenty-third chapter, titled "Description of the Sequence of the Pilgrimage to Veṅkaṭeśagiri," in the Brahmakāṇḍa, the third part of the Uttarakhaṇḍa of the glorious Garuḍa Mahāpurāṇa.
In the Śrī Garuḍa Mahāpurāṇa— Chapter 24—
Jaigīṣavya said:
O maiden, listen: as all people ascend this mountain named Veṅkaṭa, which possesses a smiling face and is meritorious, they perform the recitation of the Śrī Gītā while ascending it.
At every step, the Lord Śrīnivāsa is indeed fully, fully pleased with the host of his devotees;
by pleasing him, all attain liberation. When Hari is satisfied, O maiden, what is there that cannot be obtained?
When one hears the Purāṇa in the vicinity of a staircase, then a pilgrimage to all sacred fords and other holy sites has been accomplished;
then, during the day, they constantly glorify Hari, Śrīnivāsa, and the Guru here on the path.
Having heard of the greatness of the steps and having established a Śālagrāma there,
that virtuous woman bowed down once more and then ascended the steps.
O Lord of Birds, by ascending the stairs of those who are not Vaiṣṇavas, there is no pleasing of Hari;
rather, O King of Birds, that very act serves only to cast them further into blind darkness.
In various places, the Goddess spoke thus once more regarding Jaigīṣavya;
the maiden said:
"Jaigīṣavya is Śrīnivāsa, yet Hari is seen as Śrīnivāsa by Brahmā and the others."

"O Jaigīṣavya, out of compassion, please speak. Thus addressed, Jaigīṣavya spoke to Hari regarding the maiden Umā, daughter of Soma, and Satī; he said that Śrīnivāsa is seen by Brahmā and the other gods.

Venkatesha is seen by Rudra and the other gods as possessing a splendor exceeding that of a hundred thousand forms; Shrinivasa is seen by Rudra and the others with a radiance surpassing the brilliance of a hundred thousand suns.
The Lord of Ramā, whose splendor exceeds a thousand suns,
appears like the moon to sages and others, yet to virtuous men he is perceived directly as Hari himself.
Lord Śrīnivāsa is always perceived by the sages like a star, for Hari is directly manifest to them;
yet that Lord of Veṅkaṭa, O King of Birds, is seen by worldly beings like the sun.
Indeed, the light of Śrīnivāsa appears like a collection of blossoms to those who have entered the path of falsehood;
in the Kali age, it is seen merely as a stone, appearing with the dark-blue luster of a rock.
In the Kali age, Hari is indeed Śrīnivāsa for all men, yet the Goddess is the very form of Śrīnivāsa;
for in the Kali age, all men are characterized by tamas and rajas, and thus they do not truly recognize Him.
For those who associate with him are indeed virtuous; thus, true devotees are truly rare in the Kali age.
Those who appear to be devotees are not actually so, for they are merely intent on filling their bellies and supporting their wives. (GarP 3.24.13)
They undertake pilgrimages for that very purpose; indeed, devotion and knowledge are difficult to attain in the Kali age.
For those devotees who are never dispassionate, the vision of Hari is truly difficult to obtain.

O King of Birds, I shall describe to you the true nature of a devotee—one who is full of knowledge and exceedingly affectionate toward the Supreme, and who is not bound by hatred; listen as I correctly explain what constitutes devotion and what constitutes hatred toward you.

The constant thought that the soul, which is dependent, is distinct from Hari—who is independent, non-material, and eternally complete with knowledge and bliss—and that Hari is incomplete in his qualities; [this is the view of the dualists]. (GarP 3.24.16)

The constant concern for the honor of the gods, such as Śrī, Brahmā, and Rudra, as well as that of the twice-born, and the perpetual contemplation of the superiority of Brahmā, Rudra, and others over Viṣṇu, is indeed hatred. (GarP 3.24.17)
O Bhadrā, the great ones say that perceiving a distinction between the hands, feet, and other limbs of Viṣṇu is hatred;
likewise, the cutting or piercing of his incarnations is said to be even as the contemplation of death.
The noble ones say that hating his devotees and disparaging his words is indeed hatred itself;
and those women seen in the world who are possessed by hatred are never true devotees.
The maiden said:
"O Jaigīṣavya, tell me who these devotees are and how they manifested their devotion;
for Hari, the abode of Śrī, the Great-Souled One, is always compassionate toward the multitude of his devotees and their protector."
Thus addressed, the high-souled Jaigīṣavya, the best of devotees, spoke while recollecting the maiden.
Jaigīṣavya said:
"Prahlāda and others were devotees of Śrīnivāsa, having indeed cultivated supreme devotion toward Nṛsiṃha."
Parāśara, a devotee of the Abode of Śrī, having offered his devotion to Hari in the form of Vyāsa, subsequently attained unsurpassed sovereignty and obtained knowledge from Nṛsiṃha.

Having praised the reality of knowledge through that [teaching] and having attained it, Nārada— whose soul was nourished by devotion and who had practiced devotion toward Hari even while in the womb— went to liberation as a devotee of Śrīnivāsa.
Through that devotion he attained the status of a son of Brahmā, and through the acquisition of knowledge, he went to liberation—
namely Ambarīṣa, who was a devotee of Śrīnivāsa and who practiced devotion toward Hari, the Supreme God.
Having recited [the mantra] and attained knowledge, Durvāsas also achieved liberation, his soul nourished by that;
and Mucukunda, indeed a devotee of Śrīnivāsa, having cultivated firm devotion through dispassion, likewise attained it.

Having attained knowledge of the reality of Viṣṇu, that great-souled Puṇḍarīka, whose self was nourished by that [knowledge], obtained liberation; for he was a devotee of Śrīnivāsa who, commanded by his father, practiced devotion to Viṣṇu.
Through the grace of Hari, he whose soul was nourished by devotion attained supreme knowledge and liberation;
and Brahmā, Vāyu, Sarasvatī, and all those of upright yoga are to be known [as having likewise attained this].
They are indeed those whose devotion to Murāri is never severed, who are not attached to objects of desire, and who are pure in nature;
they are the deities known as Girīśa, Nāgeśa, and Khageśa, as well as Śukra, Ārka, Guru, Candra, Indu, and Sūrya.
Varuṇa, Agni, Manu, Dharma, Kubera, Vighneśa, the Nāsatyas, and the hosts of Maruts—
all these, including Parjanya, Mitra, and the rest, are indeed eternal devotees of Śrīnivāsa.
Viśvāmitra, Bhṛgu, Aurva, Kutsa, Marīci, Atri, Pulaha, Kratu,
Śakti, Vasiṣṭha, Sautamīya, Pulastya, and Bhāradvāja are the devotees of Śrīnivāsa.

Māndhātṛ, Nahuṣa, Ambarīṣa, Sagara, King Pṛthu, Haihaya, Ikṣvāku, Bharata, the two sons of Yayāti, Dharma, Vikukṣi, Uttāna, Bibhīṣaṇa, and Daśaratha—these were indeed men of great wisdom, and they are always remembered as devotees of the illustrious Lord of Veṅkaṭa and their Guru. (GarP 3.24.31)
The Bhāgīrathī, the ocean, the Yamunā, and the Sarasvatī;
the Godāvarī, the Narmadā, the Kṛṣṇā, and likewise the Bhīmarathī.
The Sarayū, Phalgu, Kāverī, Gaṇḍakī, and Kapilā—
these too, O beautiful lady, are devotees of Hari who reside right here.
O maiden, listen to my intention regarding this:
wherever there occurs discourse on the path of the high-souled Viṣṇu, [therein lies the truth].
Wherever Vaiṣṇavas who awaken others to the true meaning of the reality of Hari reside,
there all devotees of Viṣṇu likewise abide.
Those who perform the procession of the deity with contemplation of the Supreme Self are the devotees of Hari, and no others;
for, O Lord of Birds, in Hari, the Supreme, all the duties of the Vaiṣṇavas find their ultimate fulfillment.
Having reached Śeṣācala, he who, being devoid of devotion, does not offer food, clothing, ornaments, and the like— who indeed is a more base beast than he?

The devotees of Hari reside on the Śrīnivāsa mountain and in various places in the form of the Gaṅgā and others for the sake of serving the Wide-Strider (Urukrama); O Goddess, no worship should be performed for them.

I shall state the intended meaning there; listen to it in that context. Even those [deities] mentioned in the Purāṇas are to be worshipped individually with garments, perfumes, incense, and so forth; and having seen them, the wise man should indeed pay homage.
O Goddess, one should salute the feet of virtuous Brahmins with both hands joined in the *añjali* gesture;
likewise, one should perform an eight-limbed prostration (*aṣṭāṅga-vandana*) toward Viṣṇu and likewise toward the Guru, regarding them with the same consciousness as Viṣṇu.
One must indeed perform prostration with the eight limbs (aṣṭāṅga) to the Gaṅgā and other rivers, as well as to the tulasī plants;
likewise, one must perform obeisance to the aśvattha trees and mental obeisance to cows and other such beings.
The worship of Viṣṇu, the God of gods, must always be performed with devotion by Vaiṣṇavas alone and not by others;
O maiden, those who possess the Name, who are wise, and who are truly devoted, must always perform the worship of Viṣṇu.

O daughter, those who possess knowledge and are devoted to the Name should always perform the worship of Viṣṇu; O Goddess, for those who are devotees of Viṣṇu through the Name, no other worship of Viṣṇu need ever be performed here.
Indeed, he who worships the God of gods out of delusion and the like goes to the blinding darkness of great unrighteousness;
for Brahmā and the others gave their own names to the goddess of Viṣṇu, the Lord of the Gods. GarP_3,24.44 //
"O maiden, the wise King did not take Keśava and the others, but abandoned his own city and departed;
thus I have told you all this, O maiden—this supreme truth must be correctly embraced."
"O Govinda, Nārāyaṇa, Mādhava! You all must be propitiated by me in their entirety.
Then, O Lord of Birds, they all gathered together and once again ascended Vaikuṇṭhādri while chanting these names.
Previously chanting the names of Hari there and savoring the name of Śrīnivāsa,
they all likewise acted to behold Śrīnivāsa, making a sound like "tala" as they cried out.
Having heard these words of Kṛṣṇa, Tārkṣya said to Kṛṣṇa: "How did they taste it? Please explain this in detail. Śrī Kṛṣṇa said:
"O Śrīnivāsa, Your very name is this [taste]; indeed, the Master is the Name itself; the Master is truly the Name itself."
Because Brahmā and the other gods take refuge in her, she is therefore known by the names Ramā and Śrī.
Because he is eternally and preeminently the refuge of Ramā, Hari is known by the name Śrīnivāsa.
O Śrīnivāsa! Thus exclaiming, they dance with their hair standing on end, making sounds of clapping their hands.
"Today indeed we shall behold the face of this Hari; when shall we have accomplished our purpose?
O Keśava, having shown us your lotus-feet this very day, please show us great compassion!"
They call him Brahmā, they call him the Ancient One; they call him the one denoted by the syllable *ka*, the Lord of all worlds;
and they call him Īśa, Arha, and Rudra—the impeller in the acts of creation and dissolution.
Therefore, crying out "O Keśava! and making Hari, whose name is Keśava, dance, they went toward the pool of bliss; indeed, they went while repeatedly chanting "Nārāyaṇa! GarP_3,24.52 //
Therefore, because he is the locus of those faults, their opposites—the virtues—and the *nārāḥ*, he is Murāri;
O Lord of Birds, they call him Nārāyaṇa here in this world because of his connection with the *nārāḥ* and because all are liberated through him. (GarP 3.24.53)
O Lord of the Gods, because they are the refuge, men (nārāḥ) are so called; therefore, even more than that, he alone is Nārāyaṇa.
And those who are liberated have entered his footstep, the waters of the cosmic egg, by the mere glance of him.
O Lord of Birds, because he was born from that [Nara] and because he is always their refuge, O Lord of Heroes,
they call him "Nārāyaṇa" here in this world, for he is the creator of infinite Brahmā-eggs.
Thus they danced, praising Govinda, for there is nothing else indeed that is not his manifestation;
since all words are denotable by the word "go" (cow), and everything is expressed by all the "gobhis" (rays/words).
Therefore, O Bhīma, they always remember you as Govinda and likewise as Vedavedya;
for, filled with tears of joy, they danced before Hari, the slayer of Mura, at the sight of you.
"O Lord, grant that your servants and attendants may always reside in the fourteenth world;
for you yourself dwell thus as Vāsudeva, and here you eternally sport at all times."
Because the great ones call him "O God," they likewise call Hari "Vāsudeva.
"O Vāsudeva! they all danced at every moment, and "O Mādhava! they all danced indeed.
"O Lord of Lakṣmī," thus they all say; for the word "wealthy" (dhanin) is indeed expressive of oneself.
Therefore, the noble ones call you Mādhava; O Lord of Lakṣmī, likewise protect your devotees! (GarP 3.24.60)
Speaking thus, they danced and moved along, chanting "O Viṣṇu, protect us always and eternally!
Since you are spread everywhere, they continued chanting names such as these.
Endowed with devotion and remembering Śrīnivāsa, they all proceeded and beheld the sacred ford (tīrtha).
The maiden said:
"O Lord of Sages, what is the name of this sacred ford? O Master of the Accomplished, tell us what purpose is served here.
For whom is the Blessed Śrīnivāsa pleased at this excellent tīrtha? Speak of it in detail."
Jaigīṣavya said:
O maiden, listen; there was once a man of great intelligence named Prahlāda, the best among the devotees of Hari.
With a mind free from desire, he went to see Śrīnivāsa, who resides on the Śeṣa mountain.
At this point, the Lord questioned the sons of the Daityas regarding the true nature of Hari:
"O maiden, worship Śrīnivāsa in the form of Nṛsiṃha; human birth is very difficult to attain."
Even there, O best of Daityas, the true nature of Viṣṇu Nṛhari is very difficult to attain, and likewise is a pilgrimage;
for in whatever place such a pilgrimage occurs, the story of Hari is present.
"In that place Hari always resides, for Nṛsiṃha is indeed pervading everywhere.
Having heard this, those sons of the Daityas said to Prahlāda, the best of devotees of Hari:
"O friend, if Hari pervades all, why indeed is Nṛsiṃha not seen here in the form of water?
Being thus addressed by the sons of the Dānavas, he praised Viṣṇu with the utmost reverence.
"Reveal your true form to me, in a form suitable for the sons of the Dānavas.
Thus praised, Hari, the Abode of Śrī, assumed within that [water] a form consisting of water.
Those who perform their ablutions at this sacred ford shall possess supreme and firm knowledge;
yet, O dear one, in this Kali age, human beings will generally lack the wisdom to recognize the significance of bathing here.
Having granted the boon to the best of the Daityas, Viṣṇu vanished into a fine basin filled with water;
even today Nṛsiṃha remains within that water, as does Prahlāda together with the sons of the Daityas.
At that excellent bathing place, the sound of "Victory! is heard here and there throughout the afternoon.
This sacred ford is named Nārasiṃha; indeed, men should perform their ablutions here during the maiden period of the moon.
Having bathed in that sacred ford and having properly offered a preeminent lamp to an excellent brahmin,
they went forth again to behold Śrīnivāsa, crying out, "Govinda, Govinda!"
Having reached the place presided over by the chief vital breath (mukhyaprāṇa), the Goddess entered there and spoke:
"Tell me how Jaigīṣavya may behold Viṣṇu, the Abode of Śrī; explain that to me. (GarP 3.24.73)
Jaigīṣavya, with a joyful heart, said: "O maiden, listen as I speak this system;
having heard it from me, perform everything I have instructed. First, behold the gateway of Śrīnivāsa."
Thousands of offenses are committed by me day and night;
O God, O Supreme Person, forgive them all.
O Mādhava, reduce to ashes all my faults— mental, verbal, and even physical— in every respect, which serve as causes for hatred toward Vaiṣṇavas.
O Goddess, one should properly meditate upon the first gateway of Śrīnivāsa as indeed victory and triumph;
O Goddess, at the sacrifice of Dakṣa, one should likewise properly meditate upon Caṇḍa and Pracaṇḍa of Śrīnivāsa.
O Goddess, on the western side of Śrīnivāsa, one should remember Nanda and Sunanda with devotion; and at the left door of Śrīnivāsa, O daughter, one should remember Kumudākṣa and Kumudanta.

And when, O Goddess, shall I behold with devotion and with great reverence one who enters the body [of the Lord], having performed twelve circumambulations and remembering the Abode of Śrī at every step? GarP_3,24.79 //
O Goddess, having properly performed the ritual sipping of water (ācamana) at Śrīsvāmitīrtha, and having bathed and bowed to Bhūvarāha,
one should enter the gateway with devotion while repeatedly uttering, "Govinda, Govinda."
Afterwards, one should perform obeisance to Hari in the form of the eight-limbed prostration (aṣṭāṅga-namaskāra) and enter the temple of the deity.
Standing again at the entrance, one should contemplate with the mind the deities seated upon their thrones.
In the center, one should fully prostrate to the Śrīnivāsa-pīṭha and the goddess Nārāyaṇī;
and outside the portion of the pīṭha to the left of the deity, one should likewise pay homage to the Guru and the Deity.
O Lord of Birds, one should indeed prostrate in the south-eastern corner at the front and lower part of the pedestal;
O Goddess, in the south-western quarter, the Vaiṣṇava Vyāsadeva is always to be saluted.
With a soul nourished by devotion, one should first bow with devotion to Sudurgā in the northwest corner;
then, above the pedestal in the southeast corners, [one should offer salutations]: "Obeisance to Yama, the presiding deity of Dharma."
Above the seat, in the upper corner of the southwest (Nairṛta), one should bow to Vāyu, the lord of knowledge;
and above the seat, in the northwest (Vāyu) corner, to Subhrū and Rudra, the lords of detachment.
O Goddess, one should bow to Indra, the lord of the sovereign powers, in the northeast above the pedestal;
and here, O Goddess, one should bow to Aryaman, the lord of the Aryamans, in the southwest in front of the pedestal.
To the south of the deity and the pedestal, one should bow to Durgā, who is called Ugrarūpā;
and to the west of the pedestal, one should indeed prostrate before Kāmadeva, the lord of those who possess health.
To the north of the deity’s seat, one should remember the Lord of Rudra-devas and the non-sovereigns;
and in the center of the seat, O maiden, one should always bow to Varāha, who is known as the Supreme Puruṣa.
Above that, one should perpetually bow to Lakṣmī, who is known as Śakti and is the form of the foundation;
above her, one should bow to Vāyu and Kūrma, and above them, one should bow to Śeṣa and Kūrma.
Above that, O fair-browed one, she should indeed bow to Bhūdevatā, the presiding deity of the earth;
and above her, she should meditate upon the god Varuṇa, the sovereign lord of the Ocean of Milk.

Above that, one should indeed bow down and worship Lakṣmī and the two maidens known as Śvetadvīpa; above that, one should indeed bow down and worship the great divine Lakṣmī and the one designated as Maṇḍapa.
In the center of the pedestal, one should worship the one known as Yama and Lakṣmī; and in the middle of Yama, one should worship the Goddess.
And to the right of the god Yama, O auspicious lady, one should bow to Sūrya in the form of a lamp.
One should bow to the goddess Śrī in the form of a lamp on the left side of the god Yama,
and one should also bow to Hutāśana in the form of a lamp at the front of the god Yama.
In the presence of the God, one should bow to her named Bhūmi and constantly remember her as the presiding deity of the principle of Tattva;
and one should likewise bow to Durgā, who is the presiding deity of Tamas, in the form of the couch of Viṣṇu Śrīnivāsa.
O Goddess, one should bow to the single Self, which has the form of the steps of the pedestal facing the east;
and O Daughter, one should likewise bow to that which has the form of the steps of the pedestal of the direction situated on the right, consisting of knowledge.
O Goddess, on the eastern petal of the lotus, one should pay homage to this one called Strīrūpā and the one called Vimalā;
O Goddess, listen now as I describe the homage to Brahmā and the other deities on the petal situated in the southeast corner.
One should bow to the supreme goddess named Utkarṣaṇā, as well as to Indrāṇī, Brahmā, Vāyu, and Śeṣa;
and on the eight petals of the lotus situated in the south, one should worship those beginning with Nārāyaṇa, Ākāra, and Śeṣa.
O maiden, one must indeed perform prostration to those in female forms upon the western petal;
likewise to Gopa, Nārāyaṇa, Brahmā, Vāyu, the Brahmins and others, as well as Śeṣa, Rudra, and the rest.
One must indeed perform obeisance to those in female forms on the petals located in the northeast corner,
as well as to Īśāna, Nārāyaṇa, up to Viriñca, Vāyu, Viyat, Śeṣa, and the foremost of the gods.
One must likewise perform salutation to those in female forms and to the center of the lotus;
there resides the goddess Viṣṇu-Lakṣmī, known as Anugrahā, who is the wind, the ether, and the source of Śeṣa, Rudra, and the others.
One must indeed perform obeisance to those in female forms, for they constitute the very nature of the excellent seat of yoga (yogapīṭha).
One should always bow to the one known as Śrī Ananta, and likewise to the god who is the abode of Śrī.
A wise person should bow to Lakṣmī on the left side of Śrīnivāsa,
and to the auspicious Dharā on the right side of Śrīnivāsa.
Outside the seat, in the eastern quarter, one should bow to the auspicious Kṛpolka;
likewise, one should bow to Maholka in the south and Vīrolka in the west.
And one should pay homage to the North and to the great-souled Ulkā;
the wise person should also bow to Sahasrolka in all four corners.
One should pay homage to Vāsudeva in the east,
to the divine Saṃkarṣaṇa in the south, and to Pradyumna in the west.
In the north, one should tirelessly pay homage to Aniruddha;
and in the southeast, O auspicious maiden, one should always pay homage to Māyā.
One should pay homage to Jayā in the southwest and also to Vāyu in the northwest;
one should likewise pay homage to Kṛtyā in the northeast and to the one named Śānti in the southeast.
One should pay homage to Keśava in the east, and likewise to Nārāyaṇa;
one should offer salutations to Mādhava in the southwest and also in the northwest.
In the southeast, one should always, with devotion and self-restraint, pay homage to the auspicious Kanyaka;
likewise, one should bow to Govinda in the south and to Viṣṇu as well.
O maiden, you should pay homage to Madhusūdana in the southwest (nairṛta),
and likewise to Trivikrama and Vāmana in the west.
Then one should pay homage to Viṣṇu Śrīdhara with the syllable "Bhām";
and in the north, O Great Maiden, [one should say] "Salutation indeed to Hṛṣīkeśa."
Likewise, O beautiful lady, one should tirelessly pay homage to Padmanābha,
and one should also pay homage to Dāmodara in the northeast.
In the fourth enclosure, one should pay homage to Mahākūrma in the east;
one should offer salutation to Varāha in the auspicious southeast, O maiden.
In the south, one should pay homage again and again to Nārasiṃha and Vāmana;
with a pure mind, one should offer salutations to Bhārgava in the southwest.
Then, one should offer salutations to Mādhava and likewise to Kṛṣṇa in the west;
and one should pay homage to Buddha in the auspicious northwestern maiden [direction].
In the north, one should pay homage with diligence to you who are of infinite form in the shape of a meteor; in the northeast, one should offer salutations to the one whose form is the universe.
One should bow to Vāruṇī in the southeast, Gāyatrī in the southwest,
Bhāratī in the northwest, and Girijā in the northeast.
One should bow to Girijā on the left side, and likewise to Suparṇa; one should also pay homage to Indra in the east, together with his weapons.
"Salutations again and again to the attendant of Śrī Viṣṇu for the sake of acceptance;
'O Āgneya,' [salutations] to you, O Agni, together with your weapons," as before.
One should worship Yama in the south, Nirṛti in the southwest,
Varuṇa in the west, and Vāyu in the northwest with the words "Salutation to Vāyu."
And in the north for Kubera, and in the northeast for Śiva;
and between Īśāna and Śakra, for Brahmā together with his weapons.
And in the very center of Nirṛti, one should offer salutations again and again with "Obeisance, obeisance to Śeṣa.
Having performed the salutation in this manner, one should prostrate repeatedly.
Thus has all this been declared according to the prescribed rules regarding the vision [of the Lord]. Beyond this, however, O Lord of Ramā, one must proceed for the sake of the vision.
Having spoken thus, that goddess went joyfully with them.
O bird, the procedure for the vision of Śrīnivāsa which has been described must never be told to anyone, because it is to be kept secret at all times.
O Lord of Sages, the meeting with the virtuous who awaken one to the true nature of reality is indeed difficult to achieve;
yet, through the accumulation of merit earned over many lifetimes, he attained union with his Guru.

Just as milk abandons its own transformation and the lotus sheds its remaining filth through contact with the one whose navel is a lotus, so too, through association with the virtuous, unstable states of being and all inauspicious things shall cease to exist.

Thus ends the twenty-fourth chapter, titled "The Description of the Sequence for Ascending Śrī Veṅkaṭeśa Hill and the Names of Its Peaks and Other Features," in the Brahma-kāṇḍa, the third part of the Uttara-khaṇḍa of the glorious Garuḍa Mahāpurāṇa.
In the vicinity of the gateway to Śrīnivāsa, that goddess beheld the Svāmipuṣkariṇī along with certain others.
"O Master, O Hari, O Śrīnivāsa! she meditated upon him, the savior of Brahmā and the other gods.
For the sake of protection, Viṣṇu himself is eternally present in the waters of the Puṣkariṇī together with the gods;
therefore, they call it Svāmipuṣkariṇī, and there the maidens performed their ablutions.
O King of Birds, having become pure, the gods entered Śrīnivāsa with pure devotion to offer oblations;
and the maidens likewise performed everything exactly as instructed by their preceptor, O King of Birds.
Then Hari revealed his own form, perfectly complete and beautiful of aspect, to her;
that maiden beheld with devotion the form of Śrīnivāsa, which was delightful to her mind.
Wearing a garment variegated with gold, he was putting on a tunic together with a turban.
The fragrance of rut from the deer made the quarters of the sky fragrant;
he had eyes as broad as white lotuses, a neck like a conch shell, and mighty arms.
His body was adorned with a golden sacred thread; he was like Kandarpa himself in person, possessing a beauty that deludes the world, with limbs so tender and enchanting.
And upon seeing him, the maiden rejoiced, her beautiful limbs bristling with horripilation.
Her heart overflowing with the joy of seeing him, her eyes brimming with tears of love and horripilation, the Goddess—her faults destroyed—danced before Viṣṇu with supreme devotion:
"O Ānanda, protect me! O Mukunda, grant me happiness and protect me by bestowing liberation! (GarP 3.25.9)
Protect me always with your gracious gaze, O lotus-eyed one, moistened by the nectar of compassion!
O Govinda, O Govinda, protect me, who am deeply afflicted, forever with the gift of knowledge and other virtues.
O Janārdana, having always abandoned the most wicked associations in the form of desire and the like,
O Hari, O Hari, protect me constantly, having subdued the powerful Daityas who take the form of obstacles.
O Rameśa, protect me; O Lord of the four-faced one, Lord of the universe, Lord of Sarasvatī, protect me!
O Rameśa, protect me, you whose form is the primordial cause, whose lotus feet are worshipped by the multitudes of Vṛndārakas.
Having thus bowed with supreme reverence, he praised Viṣṇu, the supreme and ancient one,
whose countless qualities are always unknown even to Lakṣmī, O Lord.

The qualities of Hari, which are of an exceedingly vast number, are indeed unknown to Ramā; therefore, what power could there be for me in the praise of Hari? Nevertheless, I shall make an effort in praising you.
By your grace, by the grace of Ramā, by the grace of Brahmā, by the grace of Bhāratīśa, and by the grace of Rudra, I shall offer this hymn to you; nevertheless, O Viṣṇu, grant me peace.
If you are pleased with me, O Lord, grant me constant devotion at the soles of your feet;
for by the sight of you, O God, my auspicious and inauspicious karma, as well as my perpetual evil, have been destroyed.
By your māyā, this world has been destroyed; intoxicated by pride, it has become deaf and blind.
Indeed, through the power of [your] sovereignty, it has become mute toward those who are always humble, such as teachers and elders.
Do not grant me unsurpassed sovereignty, which is contrary to the lotus of Your feet;
O Lord, grant me instead the company of the virtuous who proclaim Your true nature.
O Vāsudeva, having burned away my attachment to sons and other worldly things, grant me Your lotus feet; and having burned away the anger directed toward a true Vaiṣṇava, grant me Your lotus feet.
Having burned away the greed for wealth and such things being performed, grant me [your grace] at the base of your lotus feet;
and having burned away the delusion for sons and such things being performed, grant me [your grace] at the base of your lotus feet.
Having burnt away my learning, my son, my wealth, and my pride, grant me the state of being at the base of Your lotus feet;
having burnt away my envy along with the nature of those who are true Vaiṣṇavas, protect me, O Lord of Veṅkaṭa!
And grant me a mantra, O you whose form is the primordial cause, by which there may be further union with you;
I choose nothing other than union with your lotus feet—being gracious toward me, grant that very thing to me.
Thus addressed, the gracious Lord Śrīnivāsa spoke, emitting nectar:
"O maidens, right here, recite this mantra of most secret form with supreme devotion."
I shall speak the mantra; listen today with devotion and supreme respect!
It consists of the final letter situated within [the gutturals], joined with the first [of the labials], likewise accompanied by the bindu, and joined with the first of the sparśas.
Joined with the letter *e*, ending in the first [sibilant], joined with a semi-vowel and a sibilant (*ūṣman*),
conjoined with the letter *t*, joined with a vowel, a semi-vowel, and a nasal (*antaḥstha*), and endowed with the syllable *oṃ* at both the beginning and the end.
"O maiden, by this mantra your desire shall indeed be fulfilled; there is no need for further deliberation on this matter.
Having spoken thus, Śrīnivāsa Hari revealed his true form, endowed with all its marks.
Having bowed to Śrīnivāsa, the goddess dwelt near Svāmisaras;
on that day, she gratified all the Brahmins and others with food possessing the six flavors.

In the evening, having seen Śrīnivāsa, the Goddess, together with the manifestations of Śrīnivāsa in the form of his attendants, bowed down with devotion and then performed a perfect circumambulation of Śrīnivāsa.
The goddess danced before Supratīka, casting aside her shame and crying out, "Victory! O God!
And at the time of the dance, having beheld the face of Hari with her gaze, she danced even more intensely.
O Śrīnivāsa, today my body has been purified; O Śrīnivāseśa, today my eyes have become fruitful;
and today my feet have truly become meaningful, having performed the circumambulation of you.
"Today my two hands have become meaningful, having placed the name of Murāri at their forefront.
Speaking thus and gladdening the God, she proceeded with a multitude of hymns of praise.
Then the gods' drums resounded and they rained down a shower of flowers upon his head;
at that time, the celestial courtesans performed a dance on both sides of him.
In that very same way, O Lord of Sages, they all then made the sound "tala" and performed prostrations;
on Mount Ānanda, she always causes them to dance in this manner at all times.
Immersed in bliss, that goddess also went to her own hermitage together with Jaigīṣavya.
O Lord of Sages, the noble ones say that for those who do not perform this pilgrimage in this manner, everything is fruitless.
Having gone to the hermitage together with Jaigīṣavya, he asked his guru for the mantra of Veṅkaṭeśa:
"O Jaigīṣavya, tell me the meaning of the mantra, so that it may indeed bear fruit for those who perform its recitation."
Jaigīṣavya said:
Listen, O blessed lady, to the meaning of the name Veṅkaṭeśa; having heard it, keep it firmly in your heart.
The syllable *vi* signifies the supreme; *ya* is declared to be knowledge (*jñāna*). The letter *ka* signifies bliss (*sukha*); *ṭa* is declared to be the mind (*citta*). (GarP 3.25.37)
O maiden, the state of being the Lord (Īśatva) should thus be understood as residing in the Self;
however, full knowledge, bliss, and wealth constitute the name Vyaṅkaṭa because of their all-pervasiveness.
Since the senses and so forth are said to be the "vya" (or "veṃ") because they constitute the limbs of Hari;
and since "kaṭa" has the sense of a collection, "vyaṃkaṭa" refers to the multitude of the senses.
Because he impels [the soul] toward himself, he is therefore named Vyaṅkaṭa; because he constantly sends [it] toward the object, he is therefore named Vyaṅkaṭa.
Because they consist of distinguished knowledge, the liberated ones are eternally remembered as *vyeti*;
and the assembly of the liberated is proclaimed as *vyaṅkaṭa*.
Because he is the Lord of the hosts of those eternally liberated, he is named Vyaṅkaṭa;
therefore, the individual soul (jīva), which is the subtle body (liṅgadeha), is designated as Vyaṅkaṭa.
Because he is the Lord (svāmin) of the lingas, he is designated as Vyaṅkaṭeśa;
and because the hosts of Daityas are devoid of knowledge and other virtues,
the host of Daityas is therefore proclaimed as Vyaṅkaṭa.
He who is the Lord in the withdrawal of these is therefore named Vyaṅkaṭa;
for qualities such as desire and anger are contrary to bliss.
They are proclaimed as the Vyaṅkaṭas; the Lord is their destroyer.
Therefore, knowing Him by the name Vyaṅkaṭeśa, perform your recitation. (GarP 3.25.45)
O Lord of Birds, having thus heard the greatness of Vyaṅkaṭa,
the goddess slept there that very night together with her father; and when the Brāhma-muhūrta dawned, the maiden woke up and remembered [it] in her heart.
(Prayer for the Morning of Vyaṅkaṭeśa) May Śrī Vyaṅkaṭeśa in the form of Nṛsiṃha, Śrī Varadarāja in the form of Varāha,
and Śrī Raṅgaśāyī who reclines upon Ananta, all together grant me a blessed morning. (GarP 3.25.47)
May Śrīkṛṣṇamūrti, Gadādhara, Śrīviṣṇupāda who dwells at Prayāga,
and Nārāyaṇa who resides at Śrībadarī— all of them grant me a beautiful dawn.
Dāmodara is indeed the abode of the three worlds, as are Śrī Pāṇḍuraṅga, Lord Nṛsiṃha, and Śrī Rāmadeva, whose dwelling is unfailing. O one of evil vision! 3.25.49.
May Śrī Dharmaputra, Nṛsiṃhamūrti, Śrī Pippalastha, Muhallavāsa,
Kolānṛsiṃha, and Siṃha residing at Śūrpakāra grant us vision.
May the four-faced one, the beautiful Sarasvatī, his own speech, Śarva, Suparṇa, and Śeṣa, as well as Amā, Mahendra, and those headed by Śacī, grant you prosperity.
May Dvārāvatī, Kāśī, Avantikā, Prayāga, Kāñcī, the city of Mathurā,
Māyāvatī, and the city of Hastimatī grant him his vision.
The Bhāgīrathī, the Sarasvatī, the Godāvarī, the Sindhu, the Kṛṣṇaveṇī, the Yamunā—the daughter of Kalinda—and the Narmadā likewise [purify]. (GarP 3.25.53)
The Vitastā, Kāverī, Tuṅgabhadrā, Suvajrā, Bhīmarathī, Vipāśā, Sutāmraparṇī, Pinākinī, and Kruddhā; GarP_3,25.54.
Svāmipuṣkariṇī, as well as Suvarṇamukharī,
Śrīpāṇḍavī, Taubaru, and Kapilā, which destroys all sins.
May the preceptor Vasiṣṭha, Kratu, Aṅgiras, Manu, Pulastya, Pulaha, Gautama, Raibhya, Marīci, Cyavana, and Dakṣa—may they all grant me a most auspicious dawn. (GarP 3.25.56)
May the seven oceans, the seven great mountain ranges, the seven continents, the seven groves,
and the seven worlds beginning with Bhūḥ, grant him prosperity.
May Māndhātṛ, Nahuṣa, Ambarīṣa, Sagara, King Nala, Dharmarāja, Prahlāda, Kratu-rāṭ, Vibhīṣaṇa, Gaya, Vyāsa, Hanūmān,
Aśvatthāman, Kṛpa, Umā, the daughter of Drupada, the illustrious Jānakī, Tārakā, Mandodarī, and all others constantly bring about a great morning splendor for you, O Hari!

O Lord Śrī Veṅkaṭeśa, may those forests of Aśvattha trees, as well as the groves of Tulasī and Dhātrī, O Master, the forests of Punnāga, the groves of Campaka and other flowers, the forests of Mandāra, and even the fragrant woods of Hari—may they all grant me eternal joy forever! GarP_3,25.59.
Having thus recollected Śrīnivāsa and performed her purification rites together with Jaigīṣavya, the Goddess went to the lotus pond of Hari; there, in that place, she duly performed her bath.
Having properly recited the mantra of Vyaṅkaṭeśa, she spoke to Jaigīṣavya and her preceptor.

Thus ends the twenty-fifth chapter, titled "Description of the Goddess’s Vision of and Praise for Veṅkaṭeśa," in the Brahma-kāṇḍa, the third part of the Uttara-khaṇḍa of the glorious Garuḍa Mahāpurāṇa.
The maiden said: The glorious Garuḍa Mahāpurāṇa—26.
The maiden said:
Tell me, for what purpose did Śrīnivāsa come here? Where was Śeṣācala, and when did he, the destroyer of sins, arrive? And tell me, for what reason did Svāmipuṣkariṇī come to this place? 3,26.1.
Jaigīṣavya said: Listen, O blessed and highly fortunate lady, to the arrival of Vyaṅkaṭeśa;
O Goddess, O beautiful woman, our sins shall pass away as if they were insignificant.
In ancient times, there was Hiraṇyākṣa, the son of Kaśyapa and Diti,
who served as the guardian of the second door due to the verbal censure of Sanaka and the other sages.
And in the womb of a Daitya, he became a powerful thorn to the gods;
known as Saṃjīva and Vijaya, he was a great lord devoted to Hari.
Hiraṇyākṣa, whose eyes were like those of a deer, was himself a Daitya who reviled the devotees of Hari;
such as he was, Hiraṇyākṣa prepared himself to perform austerities.
Then the goddess Diti, his mother, spoke to Hiraṇyākṣa.
Diti said:
"O illustrious one, you have been affectionate toward me since you were an eight-year-old child practicing austerities."
"Do not give me grief; he, being wise, will protect me.
I cannot live for even a moment without you, for there is no life [at all] apart from you."
"Do not torment yourself, O highly fortunate one, for my sake.
Thus addressed by his mother, Vijaya, being under her influence, spoke.
Hiraṇyākṣa said to his mother: "Abandoning this net, devote yourself fully to the service of Viṣṇu;
abandon the affection for me that has grown out of concern for your son, both in this world and in the next, whether in pleasure or in pain."
O Mother, as long as you maintain affection for me, so long will you remain in perpetual suffering.
O Mother, your notion that I am your son exists toward me, and my notion that you are my mother likewise exists toward you.
I have the notion of "father" toward my venerable father, but my notion of "husband" toward you is indeed false;
for Hari alone creates everything, and that Murāri is certainly its perfect protector.
Therefore, Hari alone is always the true mother; the motherhood of others is merely figurative.
Tell me, if motherhood were primary, who would be the mother of Droṇa and the others? You yourself would be.

If motherhood were indeed primary in you, tell me, who is the mother of Dhātṛ and the other [progenitors], from whom the world always proceeds? Therefore, Hari, Viṣṇu, the unborn and ancient one, is forever the father.
If the father were always the primary protector, tell me, who would protect the child while still in the womb?
If the protection of parents were the only standard, tell me, who would be the protectors of turtles and other such creatures?

If parents possess the quality of protectors, tell me, who are the protectors of compassion and the other virtues? Since one must experience the hell named Put, therefore the ancient Viṣṇu is the protector of his sons.
O fair-browed one, I am not the savior from hell, nor indeed is my husband, nor my father and the rest;
neither is my mother, nor my younger siblings and so forth. Viṣṇu alone is the protector of all everywhere; therefore, there is no other.
Having severed my illusion with the weapon of knowledge, you should practice the remembrance of Hari with devotion;
for that remembrance of Viṣṇu, O Mother, which is preceded by devotion, removes all sins in every way.

Or whoever performs the remembrance of Viṣṇu with devotion shall become a destroyer of sins. This body is difficult to obtain in this land of action; even there, it is rare to find worship of the form of Viṣṇu in its midst.
"Your life has passed away in vain; quickly take refuge at the feet of Śrīnivāsa.
Having thus instructed his mother, that best of sons became an ascetic due to the influence of the Daitya.
Having indeed gratified the Four-faced One with devotion, that high-souled one obtained invincibility;
then that great-souled best of Daityas, having encircled the earth with his hand, carried it away.
In the land of Śrīmuṣṭa, Hari appeared as the ancient Viṣṇu in the form of a boar;
having split the ocean, that Great-Souled One entered it and [raised up] the earth situated in the netherworld.
Having placed him upon the tip of his own tusk, he departed; and from that arrival, the chief of the Daityas came.
Striking him at the root of the ear, he slew him and restored the earth as it was before.
Having established the elephants of the cardinal directions, Viṣṇu, as the glorious Varāha, remained indeed at Śrīmuṣṭi.
Then Hari Viṣṇu reflected with devotion upon my human body today.

"Where will they worship me, or where shall I show them compassion? Having thought thus, Hari, the Lord of Beings, placed the immovable mountain known as Śeṣa upon the shoulders of Indra from the world of Vaikuṇṭha, and he himself descended to the surface of the earth.
Starting from the banks of the Suvarṇamukharī and extending as far as the Śrīkṛṣṇaveṇī, Garuḍadhvaja established that mountain.
At the tail of the mountain is Śrīśaila, while Ahobala is remembered as being in the middle;
and the mouth [of the mountain] is declared to be the sacred field (kṣetra) of Śrīnivāsa.
In this Ahobala, that which is desired through great austerities is accomplished;
for indeed, all the meritorious holy sites, such as the Gaṅgā and others, truly reside here.
Whoever constantly serves this [teaching], endowed with faith and devotion—
the seeker of knowledge shall obtain knowledge, and the seeker of wealth shall obtain wealth.
One desiring a son obtains a son, and a king regains his kingdom;
whatever a mortal desires, he attains it in every way.
Because that which is thought of is accomplished [there], they know it as the Cintāmaṇi;
and because of the abundance of lotus ponds and lakes on this mountain,
those who know the true meaning call it Puṣkarādvī.
Because its nature is that of pure gold (śātakuṃbha), they know it as Kanakādri;
and because it came from Vaikuṇṭha, it is remembered as Vaikuṇṭhādri.
Endowed with the sovereignty of nectar, he is remembered as Vyaṅkaṭādri;
indeed, [this concludes] the extent of the majesty of the mountain of Vyaṅkaṭeśa.
Even the four-faced Brahmā would not be able to describe fully those who practice supreme devotion day after day on Vyaṅkaṭādri;
even the lame would become swift of foot, and the blind would possess lotus-like eyes.
A mute shall indeed become eloquent, and one who is deaf shall become a listener;
a barren woman shall have many sons, and the destitute shall become wealthy.
All this will certainly come to pass through mere devotion to the mountain;
for who on earth truly knows the essential nature of Vyaṅkaṭādri?
For that man who knows the meritorious majesty of this mountain,
having abandoned Vaikuṇṭha— the supreme state of bliss— becomes a master of illusion (māyāvī) and rejoices together with Ramā on the banks of the Svāmipuṣkariṇī.
Salutations to you, Śrīnivāsa, the illustrious Lord of Vyaṅkaṭa, whose limbs are auspicious and wonderful, and who grants all desired objects.
O maiden, listen to the majesty of Śrī Svāmipuṣkariṇī;
within the midst of Śrī Svāmipuṣkariṇī, Śrīnivāsa is ever present.
For those who perform their ablutions there, liberation is held in the palm of their hand.
Three crores and a half crores of sacred fords in the three worlds—
all of them are eternally present at that very ford of Hari.
That sacred ford named Śrīnivāsa is saluted by all the gods;
it alone is celebrated as the temple of Śrīnivāsa.
O daughters, by the mere sight of it, sins are reduced to ashes;
by each single bath alone, association with the virtuous becomes certain.

Having attained knowledge through association with the virtuous, one finds liberation through that knowledge; this is indeed the case for those who are qualified, but the opposite is true for those who are not practitioners of yoga.
Those who believe that liberation is attained merely by bathing at sacred fords (tīrtha) should all be known as asuras; indeed, they go to the lowest state.
O two maidens, in this sacred ford of Śrīnivāsa, in the northwestern corner,
Vāyu always resides in order to perform the unsurpassed worship of Viṣṇu.
That is declared to be Vāyutīrtha, situated at a distance of twelve cubits;
it is said to measure six cubits in the west,
while Vāyutīrtha is declared to extend for six cubits in the north.
O beautiful girl, may those devotees of Viṣṇu, the foremost among the servants of Viṣṇu, perform their bath there first;
and may the compassionate Śrīnivāsa, who dwells within the honey, be forever pleased with me through this bath.
O Goddess, those who desire to bathe at Madhvatīrtha— whether they be Rudras or other great devotees of Vāyu—
always perform their ablutions there at the time of dawn, even before the sun has risen.
O maiden, those who discharge bodily waste, urine, vomit, or phlegm at the Vāyu-tīrtha,
and those who perform the purification of the anus or the penis there, are indeed asuras and rākṣasas.
O Goddess, how can I describe the merit of those who listen to the Bhāgavata Purāṇa?
And as for those, O Goddess, who mutter the eight-syllable mantra of Kṛṣṇa—the most excellent and well-guarded of mantras—[their merit is beyond measure].
Hari Keśava is exceedingly pleased with them; he dwells within the honey [of their devotion], and there is no need for further deliberation on this point.
Thus do those who indeed give gifts to the foremost of the twice-born, to the Vaiṣṇavas, and to the learned ones.
The gods do not know their merit at all; only Śrīnivāsa Hari knows it thus.
He who gives a Śālagrāma at Vāyutīrtha—Vyaṅkaṭeśa alone knows their merit.
O Goddess, bathing at Vāyutīrtha with a desireless mind is indeed very difficult for Vaiṣṇavas to attain;
yet even at that sacred site, the hearing of the Bhāgavata from the servants of Viṣṇu is obtained through the power of good fortune.
Likewise, O Goddess, at that sacred ford, it is difficult to find a gift of a Śālagrāma stone to an excellent brahmin—
one that is shaped like a jambu fruit, deep blue in color, possessing two faces, and endowed with four discs.

The great ones say that the Jānārdanī image is endowed with beautiful filaments, with banners marked by golden signs, and with *kuśa* grass, vajra symbols, and barley; a gift to her at that sacred site is difficult to obtain.
O auspicious lady, the gift of an image is the most supreme, yet it is exceedingly difficult to obtain; there should be no greed in this regard.
Likewise, the gift of a cow that has calved once and yields much milk is very rare, as is the gift of garments, jewels, and other such things.
O Goddess, the great ones say that the gift of material wealth is the most excellent, and that the gift of what one desires for oneself is likewise great;
however, they say that the gift of clothing which provides no fruit for oneself is useless.
The merit of giving a first-calf cow, which is the most excellent gift, is not obtained from cows whose milk has already been milked;
likewise, for people, it is extremely difficult to possess the supreme wisdom required for the most excellent gift of clothing.
O daughter, the book of the Bhāgavata and the Vāyu-tīrtha are most excellent and very difficult to attain;
O Goddess, the gift of wealth is most excellent, yet for men the Vāyu-tīrtha is indeed very difficult to reach.
O daughter, reflection upon Hari by Vaiṣṇavas who know the truth is truly rare, as is the Vāyu-tīrtha.
Situated to the north of the Śrīnivāsa Tīrtha is that which is called Candratīrtha; there the Moon always resides.
Remaining there, he performs the worship of Śrīnivāsa;
and in that meritorious region, O two maidens, they perform their ablutions.
They are liberated from sins such as violating the preceptor’s bed; of this there is no doubt.
Having bathed there, he who offers a *śālagrāma* stone in the eastern part [of the site], [attains the supreme goal].
One attains liberation through knowledge; there is no need for further deliberation on this point.
Furthermore, the gift of the Dadhivāmana image is extremely difficult to obtain there.
O auspicious maidens, it should be the size of a jujube fruit, round, blue in color, with a serene face, subtle, and very smooth.
It is equipped with two wheels, joined with five go-pūras,
provided with a bow and arrows, and is infinite, shaped like a coil.
The forest garland (vanamālā) is endowed with bliss and joined with a thousand heads;
it is marked by silver dots, and on the right side is the auspicious half-measure.
O Goddess, that which is accompanied by Candra is called Dadhivāmana;
such a form, which bestows great fortune upon men in the Kali age, is difficult to obtain.
O beautiful lady, know that image to be equal to Lakṣmī and Nārāyaṇa.
The gift of that form is very difficult to obtain, and hearing about it at Candratīrtha is hard to achieve;
indeed, hearing the true nature of Dadhivāmana from a Vaiṣṇava is exceedingly difficult to accomplish.
Having bathed there and heard the true nature of Vāmana, they know that the fruit of their gift is equal [to other meritorious acts].
The Candra-tīrtha is declared to be ten cubits in measure.
At that auspicious place, a bath at midday is difficult for men to obtain;
staying there, a blessed man always indeed worships Hari.
The gift of a Śālagrāma in the form of a boar is indeed rare;
it should be the size of a rose-apple fruit or like a hen’s egg.
The face of the deity is circular in shape, and its size is like that of a chickpea or similar;
it is located on the left side of the god, avoiding the middle region.
O beautiful lady, that which is joined with two wheels at the region of the head and endowed with a golden drop is called Bhūvarāha.
Having performed worship to Bhūvarāha, having given gifts to the distressed, and having also listened to the sacred recitation;
and having beheld Bhūvarāha stationed there, that man indeed has fulfilled his purpose in this world.
Having bathed there, O Goddess, whoever correctly hears the description of the Earth-Boar (Bhūvarāha) attains merit through that; he becomes a partaker of liberation—of this there is no doubt.
O Goddess, in the northeast corner of Śrīnivāsa is the Raudra Tīrtha, which is supremely purifying;
staying there, the high-souled Lord Rudra performs worship of Śrīnivāsa eternally.
They say its measure is eight cubits; there, indeed, a bath must be performed by the Vaiṣṇavas.
Having bathed there, being self-restrained, one should listen with devotion to the divine story of Murāri.
One should perform bathing, drinking, and giving of gifts there; O Goddess, Lakṣmī-Nṛsiṃha is eternally pleased [by this]. 3.26.76.
It should be the size of a jujube fruit, circular, and marked with a dot.
On the left side of the god, however, there should be two wheels,
joined with golden lines and slightly reddened.
Know that Lakṣmī-Nṛsiṃha, whose complexion is like that of a Vaiśya, whose face is radiant, and who is marked with signs such as lotus lines, bestows both worldly enjoyment and liberation.
O Lord of Sages, know that such a gift of a stone from a quarry or a carved image is difficult to accomplish;
having bathed there, one should listen with devotion to the nature of the glorious Nṛsiṃha, the Lord of Lakṣmī.
O Goddess, by the gift of an image one obtains the fruit; this is the truth, the truth—there is no need for deliberation here.
Between Īśāna and Śakra, the Brahma-tīrtha is proclaimed;
bathing there is difficult for mortals to attain, yet it accomplishes all goals.
Indeed, the gift of a Śālagrāma stone is difficult for men to obtain there;
the gift of the very form of Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇa is exceedingly rare.
The ground should be equal to an udumbara fruit; that is declared to be the proper measure.
It should be umbrella-shaped and circular, with a pleasant face and auspicious.
The mouth is said to be the size of a chickpea region,
provided with abundant [teeth] on both the left and right sides.
It should have the color of a calf from a herd of cows, be equipped with four wheels,
joined with cow-hooves, and marked with golden calluses.
Adorned with a forest garland and equipped with arrow-fletchings made of vajra—
those who know such a form of the Lord call it Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇa.
In the Kali age, O Goddess, the attainment of that [state] by men on earth is remembered as difficult to obtain; and giving gifts is even more difficult to achieve—what more need I tell you?
Having bathed at the Brahmatīrtha, one should indeed listen to the stories of Hari,
as well as those of Gaṇḍikāśilā and Lakṣmīnārāyaṇa.
Whoever understands the characteristic [of an action] will certainly obtain a result corresponding to it;
of this there is no doubt, and no deliberation is required in this matter.
To the east of the Śrīnivāsa Tīrtha is Indratīrtha;
there the Lord of Śacī remains in order to perform the worship of Śrīnivāsa.
The gift of a Śālagrāma stone should indeed be made to one learned in the Vedas;
the gift of a Śālagrāma stone destroys ten million killings.
O Goddess, O auspicious one, he who bestows upon the earth at that sacred ford a stone known as Sītārāmaśilā shall become equal to a king.
O Goddess, the Sītārāma stone is proclaimed to be of two kinds:
one endowed with five wheels, and another joined with six wheels.
In that regard as well, the one endowed with six wheels is proclaimed as the most excellent;
and for the one endowed with five wheels, the fruit is said to be twofold.
The size of a hen’s egg, very smooth and blue in color,
it is endowed with three faces and possessed of six wheels and filaments.
Adorned with golden lines and endowed with banners, vajras, and goads—
such indeed, O auspicious one, is that which is known by the names Sītā and Rāma.
O Goddess, the treasury of Sītā and Rāma, consisting of their speech and salutation, is difficult for men to attain in the Kali age; yet it is auspicious and bestows one's own sovereignty.
O Great Goddess, at Indratīrtha there is the stone known as Sītārāma;
the merit of giving a gift there is difficult to attain and is not the fruit of minor austerity.
But if one lacks the capacity for giving, one should listen to the characteristics of Hari;
one shall obtain that same fruit which results from the gift of a Śālagrāma stone.
O Goddess, in the south-eastern corner of Śrīnivāsa there exists a highly auspicious holy ford known as Vahni;
that god Vahni indeed dwells forever within the midst of that ford in order to perform the worship of Śrīnivāsa.

O Goddess, whoever performs a bath with devotion at the sacred ford known as Vahni while remembering the Unborn (Aja), attains liberation through the gateway of knowledge; O Goddess, a bath there is indeed difficult for men to obtain.
O Goddess, knowing that bathing at the king of holy fords is difficult to perform and that devotion toward it is likewise hard to find,
the gift of a *śālagrāma* stone— specifically one named Vāsudeva— is even more exceedingly rare.
Short, round, blue-colored, subtle, with a face and a pure facial disc,
joined with a beautiful flute— O auspicious lady, that which is designated as Vāsudeva is difficult to obtain as a gift in the Kali age.

O Goddess, if one lacks the capacity for that gift, then after bathing in the holy ford named Vāsudeva, one should properly hear the description of the stone; the great ones say that the fruit for those two is equal.
To the south of Śrīnivāsa, Yamatīrtha is remembered;
there resides King Yama, always performing worship of Hari.
In that place, bathing and giving gifts are remembered as being supremely inexhaustible;
O great sage, the gift of a Śālagrāma stone should be performed there.
The offering of a stone known as *paṭṭābhirāma* is prescribed;
it is as large as a mango fruit and is endowed with three faces. *GarP_3,26.108*
Deprived of its head by the discus, it was endowed with seven wheels,
blue in color, marked with golden lines, and possessed of the radiance of a cow’s tail and other such qualities.
The Paṭṭavardhana Rāma is indeed difficult to obtain and bestows great fortune;
whoever offers the Paṭṭavardhana Rāma there shall certainly become consecrated with the royal turban— of this there is no doubt.
To the southwest of Śrīnivāsa is the excellent Nairṛta Tīrtha;
indeed, Nirṛti dwells there always to perform worship.
There, one should perform a ritual bath; then rebirth no longer exists. [One should bathe] at the stone of Śālagrāma known as Puruṣottama.
That mortal who provides an image—
shaped like an udumbara fruit, with a serene face and auspicious— attains the supreme goal.
It is joined with two wheels, endowed with a wheel at the head,
marked with golden drops, and provided with a vajra-hook.
The gift of that image is difficult to accomplish, for it is therein that the high-souled Lord Śrīnivāsa is pleased;
O Goddess, when such a gift is difficult to perform, then the characteristics of that image should be heard.
Between the [shrines of] Pāśī and Nairṛta, the supreme Śeṣa-tīrtha is remembered;
having bathed there, one should present an image of Śeṣa to a twice-born man.
He goes to the supreme world, from which there is no return;
it is shaped like the fruit of the udumbara tree and is indeed spiral in form.
His speech is like that of a remainder; in him, two wheels are traditionally taught.
His fruit is joined with a single wheel and accompanied by an anthill.
Endowed with some color, the form of Śeṣa is clearly manifest to the mind;
the form of Śeṣa is said to be twofold: asleep and awakened.
The *phaṇonnatā* is fully awakened and possesses seven hundred thousand hoods;
even among those, the sleeping one is difficult to find and is remembered as bestowing great fortune.
It bestows liberation both in this world and in the next; of this there is no doubt.
It begins from the nine wheels and extends up to the twenty, wherever it may be.
He should be known as Ananta, for he bestows infinite fruit;
O fair-faced one, he should be known as Viśvambhara beyond the twentieth [chapter].
Even there, it is endowed with filaments and the single characteristic;
in the Kali age, however, that is difficult for men to obtain, and its gift is exceedingly rare.
Having bathed in the Śeṣatīrtha with a truly purified mind and having heard the description of these [sites], one attains the supreme goal.
Beyond that, O highly fortunate lady, is the supreme Vāruṇa Tīrtha;
there dwells the god Varuṇa, always performing worship of Hari.
There, one should perform a ritual bath and bestow the highest gift;
